---

## 1. Context & Operator Alignment

Build toward **today's goals → triage → prepare → admit → execute → observe → continue**, using the daily GitHub goal issue and linked individual work issues. Extend Forge's existing Conveyor, Jog, Flywheel and merge-cleanup owners.

**Explicit credit:** This proposal is intentionally informed by [OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator (AO)](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator). We are borrowing and evaluating its architectural ideas, not claiming to have invented them. No AO code has been copied, integrated or run as part of this capture. Similar concepts already exist in Forge; attribution must describe the actual influence rather than assign AO exclusive invention of general engineering patterns.

This is a bounded research/adaptation companion to #1248, #1254, #1328, #1358 and #1400, not a second outer-loop implementation charter. Read those efforts and their current branches/results before proposing code. #1400 already owns economical supervision and Conveyor composition; #1248 separates a narrow primitive experiment from real Jog execution.

The operator believes a narrowly scoped gap may be closeable over a few months. Treat that as a hypothesis, **not an engineering estimate, delivery commitment or proof of readiness**. Inference remains bring-your-own supported subscription/API access.

## 2. Recon & Code Seams

### Existing Forge owners

Local source inspected on development at `6f4dbaf9c423c9aa1b810861c9bb2a59b7851668`; this is the local recon base, not a claim of current remote parity.

- `skills/1-hourly/conveyor/SKILL.md`: prepares existing issues, capture plans, Preflight Contracts and ratings. Publishes readiness only after publication/revalidation; explicitly stops before execution admission. Its readiness label does not itself cause Jog pickup.
- `skills/2-daily/jog/SKILL.md`: serial queue, primary writer, separate full execution/publication clones, reviewed executor dispatch, receipts and supported recovery/landing.
- `skills/2-daily/flywheel/SKILL.md`: composition, operating modes, bounded repair and escalation policy.
- `utils/py/jog_run.py`: `JogSupervisorLock`, `JogCheckpoint`, `jog_run_main`, dispatch and landing boundaries. Current source already includes moved-development checkpoint reconciliation; do not scope a duplicate implementation from an older incident.
- `utils/py/releases_app.py` remains the canonical ledger writer; no direct SQL or alternate queue.
- `MACHINE-CONTRACTS.md` is the existing contract reference to consult during design.

The graph generation was 2026-09-01 and coverage reported changed/untracked metadata on relevant paths. Its old function ranges are not current evidence; direct source and skill reads were used instead. This capture is targeted reconnaissance, not an exhaustive code audit.

### Real-world evidence and its limits

- [LTVera daily goals #1094](https://github.com/BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas/issues/1094) includes executable work, optional prep, human decisions, ownership and Monday deferrals. Merely appearing in a goal issue is not permission to perform every linked action.
- [LTVera Jog closeout](https://github.com/BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas/issues/1014#issuecomment-6865843762) reports five reviewed PRs, **11 interventions and 0/4 automatic task-boundary transitions**. Agent logs/RELAY.md leftovers blocked clean-checkout admission, and an advancing integration branch rejected the final checkpoint push.
- Those are the run author's historical observations, not independently reproduced failures on current Forge. Five PRs are not five landed outcomes, and a manual recovery supervisor is not evidence of unattended progression. Recheck which defects have since been fixed before opening implementation work.

### AO findings, attribution and source references

AO main SHA resolved during capture: `53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e`. Prior discussion inspected moving-main docs/source; revalidate exact content against this pin before reuse.

- [Architecture](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/docs/architecture.md): observe external facts, persist durable facts, derive status/action; daemon/session boundaries and controller ownership.
- [Scheduler](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/backend/internal/service/automation/scheduler.go): bounded scheduled materialization, launch leases, interrupted-launch reconciliation and adoption of an existing launched session.
- [Automation queries](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/backend/internal/storage/sqlite/queries/automations.sql): deduplicated scheduled occurrences and exclusion of another active run of the same automation.
- [Lifecycle automation](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/frontend/src/docs/content/configuration/lifecycle-automation.mdx): signature-deduplicated feedback; local daemon requires an awake machine; at most three missed occurrences caught up.
- [Status](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/docs/STATUS.md): installed coding-harness integration and native account authentication. Documented capability, not a live interoperability test conducted here.

Important limitations: AO's run completion is tied to session termination, not Forge acceptance or verified landing. Scheduler deduplication is not exactly-once external execution. AO normally owns worker worktrees and PR feedback, whereas Forge owns full execution clones and its own review/landing flow. Adoption would need explicit ownership boundaries. AO does not inherently fix Forge's execution defects.

### Licensing and provenance

AO's [root license](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/53a545ad20fcd300c7c989f175f9a5c5d90fe58e/LICENSE) is Apache-2.0: permissive, including commercial modification/redistribution, with no requirement to open-source our modifications or contribute upstream. Redistribution of covered code requires the license, applicable notices, modification notices and relevant NOTICE attribution if supplied; trademark rights are not granted. Check individual files/dependencies before extraction. This capture is not a dependency-wide license audit.

Maintain explicit attribution in the eventual design doc. If code/tests are adapted, record upstream repository, exact revision/path, copied versus rewritten portions, modifications and required notices. Do not describe adapted code as original Forge work. Concepts evaluated but rejected should also have a short rationale.

## 3. Proposed Sketch & Approach

**Recommended direction:** evaluate AO's recovery patterns, then extend existing Forge supervision through current writers and commands. AO adoption remains an alternative to compare; this issue does not pre-decide a new daemon or framework.

Concepts to evaluate:
1. Observe → persist facts → decide → act. Refresh live GitHub and Forge receipts before selecting work.
2. Durable operation identity and recorded intent before dispatch; reconcile an existing attempt before launching again.
3. Explicit never-started / running / finished / uncertain recovery outcomes. Never blindly repeat an ambiguous external action.
4. Waiting is distinct from failure: exclude held/dependent items during pre-admission selection. For already-admitted work, use Jog's supported parking/continuation behavior under its existing lock; do not add parallel execution or a second queue to bypass a blocked head.
5. Deduplicate unchanged feedback/wakes; prefer existing event/timer facilities over token-consuming agent polling.
6. Bound tasks, wall time, spend and repair attempts per wake; preserve the next action and evidence.

Compose the existing owners:
- Selected daily goal issue and linked work → bounded triage.
- Conveyor → published, revalidated preparation.
- Explicit supported Jog admission → current executor/reviewer/gates.
- Existing authorized merge-cleanup → landing and reconciliation.
- Existing receipts and GitHub truth → report/next eligible work.

Scheduling metadata, if needed, must reference existing operations; it must not become a second queue, lease owner or completion ledger. Model interpretation proposes work; deterministic code enforces admitted scope, identities, budgets and holds. Reuse Flywheel's existing repair/escalation policy instead of adding approval ceremony for routine authorized recovery.

### Ownership of this research and proposed downstream gates

This issue owns the attributed AO comparison, current-state gap map and recommendations. Implementation and execution trials below belong to the existing #1400/#1248 efforts or explicitly scoped follow-ups agreed during the ownership map; they are not a second implementation plan here. This research can close with an evidence-backed handoff even while downstream trials remain open.

AO's Go daemon is an always-running runtime supervisor; its CLI is a client. Forge's tick is an event-log/claim coordination kernel, not a direct equivalent of AO's complete daemon. Borrowing supervision concepts does not imply replacing tick or adding an always-on process. Evaluate existing native wake facilities first.

### Proposed downstream investigation and delivery gates

1. Map each proposed concept to existing code and the related issues/branches; classify already present, defective, missing or deliberately excluded. Establish the current baseline before implementation.
2. Prove two already-prepared Jog tasks advance without manual intervention; resolve only reproduced transition defects through their existing owners.
3. Define the smallest Conveyor-to-Jog handoff, including publication, explicit selection/admission, dependencies and preserved holds. Do not make a readiness label authority.
4. Add daily-goal interpretation initially for a named issue and bounded explicit issue IDs. Revalidate live states and goal revisions before acting; a new comment cannot silently expand authorization.
5. Reuse existing wake infrastructure and exercise interruption at intent persistence, dispatch, result recording and publication. Preserve uncertain outcomes and local evidence.
6. Run bounded real-day trials after authorized disposable acceptance runs; record useful deliveries, automatic transitions, interventions, duplicate attempts, stuck waits, elapsed time and known/unknown inference cost.

Trade-off: a thin Forge extension preserves established ownership but leaves us responsible for integration recovery. AO adoption offers a mature-looking local control surface but introduces worktree/session/PR ownership integration. Compare both against observed effort, not marketing or an unsupported calendar estimate.

Rollback: disable new automatic selection/wakes and return to explicit Conveyor/Jog/Flywheel invocation, preserving queue rows, leases, receipts, branches and local-only evidence. Never clear state to make a demonstration pass.

## 4. Acceptance & Non-Goals

**This research issue closes when** the attributed comparison, current-state ownership/gap map, licensing/provenance recommendations and bounded next experiment are documented and handed to their existing owners. The implementation/trial criteria below are proposed qualification criteria for those downstream efforts, not claims that filing this issue authorizes or completes them.

- [ ] AO attribution and exact reference revisions retained; any eventual code reuse has a provenance/license review.
- [ ] Existing outer-loop issues/branches reconciled into one ownership map; no competing supervisor plan, queue or ledger.
- [ ] Historical LTVera failures checked against current source; already-fixed defects are not represented as missing features.
- [ ] A recorded baseline distinguishes prepared, reviewed PR, merged and acceptance-verified outcomes.
- [ ] Two disposable work items from one explicit daily goal advance through existing preparation/admission/execution interfaces, with one dependency wait and one supervisor restart.
- [ ] No duplicate admission/execution, no held/future/human-owned work dispatched, no unsupported replay after an uncertain effect.
- [ ] Restart exercises cover before/after dispatch and before/after result persistence; supported recovery preserves existing records.
- [ ] An independent eligible item progresses while another waits; tests follow repository policy and run in safe isolation.
- [ ] Scope/time/spend/attempt limits and stop behavior are observable; missing cost telemetry is marked unknown.
- [ ] Every manual or agent-assisted repair is recorded. Two PRs produced through manual restarts do not count as unattended success.
- [ ] A bounded trial report recommends extend Forge, adopt AO with an adapter, narrow the scope, or stop—with evidence and unresolved risks.

### What it's not

- No claim of a novel supervision architecture, AO-equivalent product, exactly-once execution or proven unattended factory.
- No approved implementation schedule; “a few months” remains an unvalidated planning hypothesis.
- No replacement of Conveyor, Jog, Marathon, reviews, merge-cleanup or canonical writers.
- No desktop/mobile/terminal-hosting rebuild or broad harness-support project.
- No automatic authorization to push, merge, deploy, modify remote servers, spend beyond caps or obtain new credentials.
- Filing this research issue does not start implementation, install AO, schedule jobs, migrate state or run live factory experiments.

Recon: 6f4dbaf9c423c9aa1b810861c9bb2a59b7851668 · local base: development · review: independent Agy/Gemini draft review plus author source reconciliation; reviewer could not access the Forge checkout (sandbox denial), so no independent source verification is claimed.
title: Research: adapt Agent Orchestrator's durable supervision concepts to Forge's daily-goals loop (explicit attribution)

body:
## Executive summary

`CHANGELOG.md` is the file PR branches conflict on most. Every PR adds an entry, so whenever one PR lands, every other open PR that also adds an entry conflicts. Merge-cleanup's B1 repair can resolve these conflicts, but each repair pushes a new head. That new head needs fresh checks and a re-pin, and the PR is deferred to the next run (`SKILL.md` Phase 5). This issue proposes that PR branches stop editing `CHANGELOG.md`. The author writes the entry in a **Changelog** section of the PR body. The existing post-merge reconcile writer, which already runs once after each merge with one writer at a time, copies that section into `CHANGELOG.md` in its reconcile commit. Nothing new is added to PR branches, there is no fold step, and that whole class of conflict goes away.

- **High:** in a downstream consumer repo, 40 of the last 50 merged PRs edit `CHANGELOG.md` (Oct 30 to Nov 15).
- **High:** in that repo's 2026-11-14 batch, PRs that merged cleanly landed 11 to 37 minutes apart. The one PR held up only by a `CHANGELOG.md` conflict waited 4 h 13 min.
- This is the `CHANGELOG.md` counterpart of #1458, which proposes the same "written at landing" default for `releases.db` / `releases.sql`.

Filed as an idea to revisit. It does not authorize implementation. Rating and ledger row are deferred to pickup (decision 6).

## 1. Context

Today PDDA asks for one dated `CHANGELOG.md` entry per substantive iteration, using the "default per-PR format" `## YYYY-MM-DD — <Summary> (GH-N)` (`PROJECT/PDDA.md`, "CHANGELOG.md — end-of-iteration record"). B1's `union_changelog` can merge two prepended dated sections (GH-789), but only by repairing the PR branch. Under an unchanged per-PR policy, every repair costs a push, a CI run and a re-pin.

### Evidence (one downstream consumer repo, aggregate)

**Per-file churn, last 50 PRs merged into the integration branch (2026-10-30 to 2026-11-15):**

| File | PRs touching it |
|---|---|
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 40 / 50 |
| `releases.db` | 24 / 50 |
| `releases.sql` | 24 / 50 |
| generated release preview HTML | 21 / 50 |
| retired `RELEASES.md` (now a generated view) | 0 / 50 |

**The 2026-11-14 batch:** 13 small PRs (docs, chores, tests, small reviewed code changes), landed `direct` with the GH-1383 canary.
- **Merged so far:** 9 in 7 h 8 min (first merge 10:46, ninth 17:54 local time). 4 PRs were still open at the end of the day.
- **Commits on the integration branch:** 19 in total, 9 merges plus 10 reconcile or record commits.
- **Hosted push CI:** 14 runs. 10 were cancelled by the concurrency group, 4 succeeded and 1 was pending.
- **Dry-run forecast:** 10 of 12 PRs merged cleanly on their own, but it printed "9 of 12 PRs conflict". Every pairwise conflict involved one of two hub PRs: one conflicted on `CHANGELOG.md`, the other on `releases.db`/`.sql`. #1470 / PR #1472 address that forecast gap.
- **Earlier history:** the same repo recorded one ledger-only conflict on a single PR re-created seven times in two days, once by each landing (see #1458).

### Why the PR body and not git history

- **Squash commits keep only commit text.** In that repo's squash-merge setup (`squash_merge_commit_message = COMMIT_MESSAGES`), one example PR's squash commit body is two lines of commit text. Its changelog entry adds the affected file, the finding and three related issue links. Its PR body adds the verification steps and what was left out of scope.
- **Squash commit quality varies.** Another PR's squash body was only relay-turn commit subjects.
- **So rebuilding the changelog from `git log` loses information today.** The richest record is the PR body, and that lives only on GitHub.

## 2. Recon and code seams

- **`utils/py/wave_reconcile.py` already reads the PR body.**
  - `fetch_pr_metadata` (around L369-388) calls `gh pr view N --json number,title,state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,...,body,...`, with an `--offline-manifest` path.
  - It already writes docs idempotently with a rollback journal (`record_merge_evidence`, around L351).
  - It runs once per merged PR, after the merge, on the integration branch (merge-cleanup Phase 5; `[skip ci]` intermediate reconciles since GH-1383).
  - It does not write `CHANGELOG.md` today.
- **B1:** `ledger_merge.py` `union_changelog` and the B1 path set (`releases.db`, `releases.sql`, `LEADERBOARD.*`, `RELEASES-PREVIEW.html`, `CHANGELOG.md`).
- **PDDA:** `pdda.sh changelog` is warn-only, so it nudges and never blocks (`PROJECT/PDDA.md`).
- **#1458:** the per-repo `.pdda-mode` setting (`LEDGER_WRITES=landing|branch`) for the ledger.
- Recon was against the vendored copy in a downstream repo (`.xyz/` snapshot of 2026-11-09 to 11-14), not Forge `development`. Line numbers are approximate.

## 3. Proposed design (preferred): the entry lives in the PR body, the reconcile writes it

1. **PR template.** Add a short section:
   ```
   ## Changelog
   <one to five lines: what changed, why, how it was verified>
   ```
   The reconcile owns the heading (`## <merge date> — <summary> (GH-N)`). The author writes only the body. Where the summary comes from (the first line, or the PR title) is open decision 3.
2. **Extraction.** Take the text under `## Changelog` up to the next level-2 heading or the first HTML comment block. Review bots append their own sections and comment blocks to PR bodies, and this keeps them out. Insert it as plain Markdown text. Strip HTML comments and conflict markers, and refuse a section that contains a level-1 or level-2 heading. A PR body is untrusted input and is never executed.
3. **Writer.** `wave_reconcile.py` prepends the entry to `CHANGELOG.md` in the same reconcile commit and journal it already uses. The entry carries a hidden `<!-- pr:N merge:<sha> -->` marker, so a second run finds the marker and writes nothing, and the entry stays append-only. It uses the existing PDDA date-first heading, so B1's `union_changelog` and existing heading checks keep working for legacy or opted-out repos.
4. **Edge cases:**
   - **No section in the body:** fall back to the PR title as a one-line entry. Flag it as `changelog: fallback-title` in the reconcile output and the batch issue, so someone can append a dated correction.
   - **Body edited after merge:** the reconcile captures the body at reconcile time, right after the merge. Later edits do not change history. A correction is a new dated entry (PDDA append-only rule).
   - **Transition, PR still edits `CHANGELOG.md`:** if the PR already added an entry naming its GH-N, the reconcile writes nothing for it, so there is no duplicate.
   - **Offline or `--offline-manifest` runs:** use the manifest's `body` field. If it has none, use the title fallback and the flag.
   - **Direct or express commits with no PR:** keep today's behaviour, where the commit writes its own entry.
5. **`CHANGELOG.md` stays committed.** Agents and offline clones read it, and skills tell agents to check it before starting work.
6. **Opt-in.** Add a `.pdda-mode` key alongside #1458, for example `CHANGELOG_WRITES=landing|branch`, with `branch` as today's behaviour. Alternatively it could go in `.merge-cleanup.json`, but the writer is the PDDA reconcile, so `.pdda-mode` fits better. Under `landing`:
   - an optional PR-side check warns, without blocking, when a branch edits `CHANGELOG.md`;
   - `pdda.sh changelog` judges freshness on the integration branch after the reconcile, not on PR branches.
7. **`releases.db` / `.sql` are out of scope here.** They are binary or dump files that the reconcile already writes. Whether PR branches should write ledger rows at all is #1458's question. A "Ledger" section in the PR body could carry a constrained declarative form there, for example `rated N/N/N/N` or `close GH-N`, parsed and never executed. That is left to #1458.
8. **Optional repo setting, outside the harness:** set the squash commit message to `PR_BODY`, so every squash commit carries the full entry and the changelog can be rebuilt from `git log` alone. Trade-off: this changes every future squash commit, and bot-appended text lands in history unless the PR template keeps bot output out of the body. This is each repo's decision, not a harness default.

### Alternative: per-PR fragment files

Each PR adds `changelog.d/GH-N.md` (front matter: GH number, date, summary). The reconcile folds the fragments into `CHANGELOG.md` and deletes them, ordered by merge commit time and deduplicated by GH-N.
- **Pros:** the entry is reviewed in the diff and lives in git without GitHub.
- **Cons:** a new directory, a fold-and-delete step, and fragments left behind by abandoned or reverted PRs.

Preferred only if a repo must not depend on GitHub at reconcile time. It already does, because `fetch_pr_metadata` calls `gh pr view`.

## 4. Interaction with merge-cleanup

- **B1:** `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts no longer happen for opted-in repos. B1 stays in place for the ledger, legacy branches and opted-out repos. Fewer B1 runs means fewer new heads, fewer deferrals (exit 3) and fewer re-pins.
- **GH-1066 grouping:** shared `CHANGELOG.md` edits were already "not proof of semantic coupling". With them gone, more queues come out clean under `direct`, and grouping is kept for real code coupling.
- **Landing forecast (GH-1452, #1470 / PR #1472):** changelog-only hubs disappear. The forecast could label a `CHANGELOG.md`-only conflict on an opted-in repo as "resolved by landing mode" instead of counting it.
- **Reconcile failure after a merge:** the same open question as in #1458. The writer must be resumable, and a failed write must be visible in the batch record.

## 5. Risks

- **Reconcile needs GitHub:** it already does today. The offline manifest path covers outages.
- **Entry quality:** entries are reviewed in the PR body instead of the diff. Mitigation: the template section, plus the fallback flag.
- **Mixed fleet during migration:** the transition rule (no duplicate when a branch already wrote an entry) covers PRs opened before the switch.
- **Untrusted PR text in a committed file:** text only, sanitized as above, never executed.

## 6. One-week trial and exit criteria

- **Trial:** one downstream repo opts in for one week, with the PR template section and the reconcile writer behind `CHANGELOG_WRITES=landing`.
- **Measure:**
  - `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts per landing (target 0);
  - B1 repairs, new heads and re-pins per batch;
  - time from ready to merged;
  - `fallback-title` count;
  - duplicate or missing entries, found by checking the GH-N markers against merged PRs.
- **Keep it if:** there are zero changelog conflicts, zero duplicate or missing entries, and B1 repairs fall by at least the share caused by `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Roll back if:** an entry is lost or duplicated, or the reconcile fails to write and nothing notices. Rollback is one config key.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With `CHANGELOG_WRITES=landing`, a merged PR with a `## Changelog` section produces exactly one dated entry in the reconcile commit, carrying the `pr:N` marker.
- [ ] Re-running reconcile for the same PR writes nothing.
- [ ] A PR without the section produces a title entry and a `fallback-title` flag in the reconcile output and batch issue.
- [ ] A PR that still edits `CHANGELOG.md` produces no duplicate.
- [ ] With the key absent or set to `branch`, behaviour is unchanged.

## What it's not

- Not a change to `releases.db` / `.sql` writes. That is #1458.
- Not a new merge-cleanup mode or gate bypass.
- Not removing `CHANGELOG.md` from git, and not making GitHub the source of truth for history.
- Not a weekly integration branch. That was evaluated and rejected: it moves the same conflicts to a second branch, needs PRs retargeted (GH-1066 step 7 requires separate authorization) and a second reconcile, and stops closing keywords from firing until the weekly landing.

## Open decisions

1. `.pdda-mode` key or `.merge-cleanup.json` key for the opt-in.
2. Whether the reconcile writes one entry per PR, or one entry per batch listing every PR.
3. Where the summary line comes from: the PR title, or the section's first line.
4. Whether the harness should recommend the `PR_BODY` squash setting, or only mention it.
5. Whether `pdda.sh changelog` gains a PR-side "branch edits CHANGELOG.md under landing mode" warning.

Related: #1458, #1470, PR #1472, GH-789, GH-1066, GH-1383, GH-1452.

Downstream counterpart (project-specific detail, trial plan and decisions): https://github.com/BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas/issues/1103

`Recon: downstream vendored .xyz snapshot (2026-11-14) · base: not Forge development (unverified against current Forge) · review: consult not run`
title: PDDA: the landing reconcile writes CHANGELOG.md from a Changelog section in the PR body, so PR branches stop editing it

body:
## 1. Context & Operator Alignment

**Problem.** `relay-automation/xyz-vendor.sh` has two tiers: Tier 1 (core harness) and Tier 2 (`--with-releases`, Tier 1 plus the ledger overlay). Both mirror all of `relay-automation bin src utils test skills` into `<host>/.xyz/`. That is about 20 MB and 1,760 files in BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas. A host repo that only wants the **ledger** (the `releases.db` / `releases.sql` CLI, post-merge reconciliation and PDDA doc checks) still gets every skill, relay shim, marathon runtime, tick core and test suite.

**Operator ask.** Add a vendor flag that copies **only the ledger system** into the host repo: ledger CLI, reconcile scripts and PDDA checks, with their real import closure. No skill files, relay or marathon runtime, tick, or harness tests.

**Why now.** Hosts such as LTVera use `.xyz/` mainly for `releases_app.py` and `wave_reconcile.py` (see their AGENTS.md / OPERATIONS.md); LTVera research found the product code itself (app, CI, Docker, tests) does not depend on `.xyz/` at all. The full overlay brings drift, re-vendor churn (#1011, #715, #1013) and extra surface for agents to wander into. The companion LTVera research issue (linked in a comment) checks whether LTVera needs the overlay at all.

## 2. Recon & Code Seams

Recon at `development@776b1c5b6`.

- **Tier logic:** `relay-automation/xyz-vendor.sh`
  - `:37-46`: flag parsing (`--no-register`, `--with-releases`).
  - `:66-72`: Tier 2 is turned on automatically, and kept on, when `releases.db` exists at the host root.
  - `:432-433`: `VENDOR_DIRS` and the `RELEASES_OVERLAY` deny-list (GH-197).
  - `:435-505`: `materialize_vendor`. It stages a full mirror, then removes items from the deny-list. It checks that `bin/tick` and `relay-turn-lib.sh` exist (`:466-468`), writes `VERSION tier=1|2` (`:478`), and keeps the host-owned `XYZ_RUNTIME_PATHS` (GH-312).
- **Re-vendor path:** `relay-automation/xyz-sync.sh:296` runs `"$VENDOR_SCRIPT" <repo>` **with no flags**. With the auto-detect at `:66-72`, any `xyz-sync update` would turn a ledger-only install back into a full Tier 2 overlay. **The mode must persist across re-vendors.**
- **Ledger import closure** (`utils/py`):
  - `releases_app.py` imports `harness_paths` (`:4718`). It also has lazy imports of `work_connectors/` (`:1636`, `:5505`, `:5904`, `:5936`) and `jog_run` (`:5201-5238`, only for the jog subcommand).
  - `wave_reconcile.py` imports `harness_paths` (`:26`), `gate_env` and `proc_group` (`:668-669`), and `releases_app` (`:1164`, `:1670`, `:1693`).
  - `wave_reconcile.py` also shells out to non-ledger tools through `harness_tool()`: `marathon_plan.py` (`:1970`), `timeline/export_timeline.py`, `leaderboard.sh` and `marathon-plan.sh` (`:2005-2007`). It runs the host's own `utils/ci-route.sh` (`:480`, `:638`). Its PDDA gate (`:2098`) picks `utils/pdda-local-checks.sh` or `utils/pdda/pdda.sh`. `leaderboard.sh` already skips when absent (`:2040-2043`). The others need the same treatment.
  - `harness_paths.py`, `gate_env.py` and `proc_group.py` use only the standard library.
  - `releases_cycle.py` uses only the standard library.
- **PDDA:** `utils/pdda/` (pdda.sh, pdda-lib.sh, templates, check_* .py) and `utils/pdda-local-checks.sh`.
- **Registry / HQ:** `register_vendor` writes `registry.tsv`. `xyz-sync check` drift compares `tick_version` and `source_commit`, so a ledger-only install without `bin/tick` needs a defined `tick_version`. `utils/hq/hq.sh:607` treats a repo as "Tier A" when it has a vendored XYZ install, so it must not take a ledger-only install for a full harness.
- **Existing tests to extend:** `test/gh197-vendor-tier-split.sh`, `test/gh105-vendor-releases-addon.sh`, `test/gh312-vendor-preserves-state.sh`, `test/gh358-wave-reconcile-vendored-paths.sh`.

**Blast radius:** xyz-vendor.sh, xyz-sync.sh (persisting the mode), wave_reconcile.py (optional-tool skips), the hq Tier A check, and vendor tests. Default Tier 1 / Tier 2 behaviour must not change.

## 3. Proposed Sketch & Approach

**Revised after the consult.** The first draft said to skip the planner and timeline steps when their tools are absent. Codex showed that `utils/releases-merge-resolve.sh:200-221` also calls those tools, and that adding missing-tool tolerance to `wave_reconcile.py` would change Tier 1/2 failure behaviour (`wave_reconcile.py:2057-2061`). Instead, the ledger tier **ships every tool that reconcile and merge-resolve call**. The LTVera research ran the planner on this subset successfully.

1. **Flag:** `xyz-vendor.sh <host> --ledger-only` writes `VERSION tier=ledger`. It cannot be combined with `--with-releases` (exit 2).
2. **Allow-list manifest** for this mode only. Tier 1/2 keep the GH-197 deny-list.
   - **Ledger:** `utils/py/{releases_app,releases_cycle}.py`, `utils/releases-merge-resolve.sh`, `utils/release-lanes.sh`, `RELEASES-DB-FAQS.md`.
   - **Connectors** (loaded lazily on ledger writes, `releases_app.py:1636`): `utils/py/work_connectors/`, plus `utils/py/device_config.py` (`work_connectors/__init__.py:35,95`) and `utils/py/board_sync.py` (`work_connectors/github_board.py:58`).
   - **Reconcile:** `utils/py/{wave_reconcile,harness_paths,gate_env,proc_group}.py`.
   - **Planner step** (fatal on failure, `wave_reconcile.py:2059`): `utils/marathon-plan.sh`, `utils/marathon-plan-zones.default.json`, `utils/py/{marathon_plan,_marathon_plan,router_audit}.py`.
   - **Views:** `utils/timeline/` (export_timeline.py and template) and `utils/leaderboard.sh`. merge-resolve calls both when the host has adopted those views.
   - **PDDA:** `utils/pdda/`, `utils/pdda-local-checks.sh`, `utils/py/{pdda_gov_scan,pdda_comment_refs}.py` (`pdda.sh:1216,1350`).
   - Plus the `package.json` boundary and `VERSION`.
   - **Guard against a silently dropped file (the GH-77 failure behind GH-197's deny-list):** a closure test walks every manifest `.py` recursively. It covers top-level and lazy imports, package files, and `harness_tool()` / `$HERE/…` subprocess targets, and fails on any module or tool missing from the manifest. Only an explicit exemption list passes: currently just `jog_run`.
3. **Persist the mode:** with no tier flag, `xyz-vendor.sh` reads the existing `.xyz/VERSION tier=` first, and `tier=ledger` beats the `releases.db` auto-promotion at `:66-72`. Explicit `--with-releases` upgrades to Tier 2. `--ledger-only` on a Tier 2 install downgrades it, and the GH-312 runtime-state preservation still applies. `xyz-sync update` (`:296`) needs no change.
4. **Mode-aware runnability check:** under `tier=ledger`, skip the `bin/tick` and `relay-turn-lib.sh` checks (`:466-472`) and check the manifest entry points instead.
5. **PDDA host-root resolution:**
   - `utils/pdda/pdda-lib.sh:6` defaults `PDDA_REPO_ROOT` to two directories up, which is `<host>/.xyz` when vendored. It must resolve to the git toplevel of the host, so it scans the host's PROJECT/.
   - `wave_reconcile.py:2098` only looks at host-root `utils/pdda*`. It should keep preferring a host-owned copy (LTVera ships its own `utils/pdda/`) and fall back to `harness_tool()`.
6. **Jog without the jog runtime:** guard the three `jog_run` call sites (`releases_app.py:5198-5241`: `cmd_jog_run`, `_jog_verb_dispatch`, `cmd_jog_land`). Every jog verb must exit non-zero naming `tier=ledger`, not raise `ModuleNotFoundError`.
7. **Registry and drift check:**
   - Store the tier in `registry.tsv` in a way that keeps old 5-field rows parseable (`xyz-vendor.sh:214`, `xyz-sync.sh:178`).
   - `xyz-sync check` must not report `tick_version` drift (`:423,430`) or `SAFETY GUARD MISSING` for `relay-drive.sh` (`:88,434-452`) on a ledger row.
8. **HQ:** filter ledger-tier rows in `hq_xyz_lookup` / `hq_tier` (`utils/hq/hq-lib.sh:69-136`). Then `hq status`, `park`, `queue`, `fire` and `next` (`hq.sh:121,248,531,605,647`) all agree that a ledger-only repo is not Tier A for driven lanes.
9. **Docs:** usage line, a tier table in the xyz-vendor.sh header, and notes in UPGRADE.md and RELEASES-DB-FAQS.md.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Skip missing tools inside reconcile.* Rejected: it changes existing tiers and doesn't cover merge-resolve.
- *Package the ledger as a pip module.* Deferred.
- *Move the ledger out of the repo.* That is #1224, which is complementary.
- *No vendoring; run from an external XYZ-forge checkout with `--root`.* That works for the writer (LTVera `docs/qa/gh720/verification.md:17`) but is unproven for reconcile, and it gives up VERSION pinning.

**Risk / rollback.** An additive flag. Re-run with `--with-releases` to restore Tier 2.
- The planner needs Python ≥3.10: `_marathon_plan.py:121` raises `TypeError` on the system 3.9.
- The file list may still miss a non-Python asset. The research's first pass missed the zones JSON and the HTML template, so the closure test must cover data files read by path.

## 4. Acceptance & Non-Goals

- [ ] `xyz-vendor.sh <tmp-host> --ledger-only` produces `.xyz/` with **no** `skills/`, `bin/`, `src/` or `test/`, at most ~30 files, and `VERSION` contains `tier=ledger`.
- [ ] In that host, with the XYZ-forge checkout made unreachable (no harness-home fallback):
  - `releases_app.py check` exits 0 on a seeded fixture ledger.
  - A ledger write does not print `ModuleNotFoundError` on stderr. This fails today without `device_config` and `board_sync`.
  - A **non-dry-run** `wave_reconcile.py --pr <N> --skip-branch-check` against offline landing metadata exits 0. It runs the planner, the timeline (with `RELEASES-PREVIEW.html` present) and the PDDA gate.
- [ ] PDDA vendored at `.xyz/utils/pdda/` scans the **host** PROJECT/. A deliberately broken host capture doc makes it fail, not exit 0 against an empty `.xyz/PROJECT`.
- [ ] `releases-merge-resolve.sh` resolves a conflicted `releases.sql` in a host that has adopted `RELEASES-PREVIEW.html` and `LEADERBOARD.md`.
- [ ] The closure test fails when `device_config.py` is removed from the manifest. That proves it follows imports inside packages.
- [ ] After `--ledger-only`, running `xyz-sync update <host>` with no flags and `releases.db` present keeps `tier=ledger`. This fails on today's code, which auto-promotes to Tier 2.
- [ ] `xyz-sync check` on the ledger row reports no drift and no `SAFETY GUARD MISSING`. `hq fire` refuses the repo as not Tier A.
- [ ] `--ledger-only --with-releases` exits 2. Explicit `--with-releases` on a ledger install upgrades to Tier 2.
- [ ] `releases_app.py jog run --dry-run` exits non-zero with a message naming the missing tier, not a traceback.
- [ ] Existing `gh197`, `gh105`, `gh312` and `gh358` vendor tests stay green, so Tier 1/2 output is unchanged.

**What it's not**
- **Not** a change to Tier 1/2 contents, or to `wave_reconcile.py` failure behaviour on existing tiers.
- **Not** removing `.xyz/` from any host. Whether LTVera needs the overlay at all is the companion LTVera research issue.
- **Not** packaging the ledger as a pip/npm module, and not moving it out of the repo (#1224).
- **Not** changing when the ledger writes (#1458).
- *Deferred:*
  - Splitting `wave_reconcile.py` into ledger and planner halves, which would let the ledger tier drop the planner.
  - Shipping `jog_run` in the ledger tier.

title: xyz-vendor: --ledger-only mode that vendors only the ledger, reconcile and PDDA scripts (no skills/relay/marathon)

body:
## Problem

In a host repo relay run (BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas#981) the AI reviews (a) turned a FAIL with open findings into a PASS with no new evidence, and (b) approved without running anything, relying on the builder's own receipts. A human reviewer caught it.

Two gaps in the relay harness allow this:

1. **Reviewer protocol text.** The scaffolded protocol says "A `[Blocker]` must cite an observed failure" but says nothing about a finding carrying over between rounds.
2. **`relay_drive.py` `judge_terminal` (GH-1428).** When `MARATHON_REVIEWER_GATE_CMD` is set, the approval is refused only if the builder declared unverified work and the reviewer's own `gate run:` line is not `yes — exit 0`. The driver trusts that declaration; nothing runs.

## Operator rulings (pipeline owner)

- Keep the existing `[Blocker]` rule and add next to it, verbatim: "A finding from an earlier round stays open, and the verdict stays failing, until new evidence closes it."
- The driver runs the configured gate command itself and records the exit code, instead of trusting the reviewer's "gate run: yes" line.

## Scope

- `relay-automation/new-relay.sh` and its mirrors of the rule text (marathon brief step 4c, relay and relay-xyz skills).
- `utils/py/relay_drive.py` approval branch: run the configured command through the existing `gate_env` / `proc_group.run_bounded` helpers, record command and exit code on stderr and in the attestation, refuse on non-zero.
- No behaviour change when no gate command is configured. No new suite (GH-831); manual check retained under `TESTS-RESULTS/`.

## Non-goals

- No new config file, env framework, clone manager or scheduler.
- Does not rerun browser cases or anything outside the configured command.

Refs BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas#981, #1428.
title: relay-drive: run the configured reviewer gate itself on Approved; add finding-continuity rule to the reviewer protocol

Claude Prompts.md` and `rebalance.db` into `temp/daily-log/YYYY-MM-DD.log`; it is distinct from the GitHub repo-level `/daily-planner` skill. |

## Diagnosis / existing gap

Operators starting their workday across XYZ Forge (dogfood maintenance) or repos where XYZ Forge is vendored (`.xyz/`) lack a shared, per-day GitHub coordination ledger issue that bridges yesterday's unfinished work, newly assigned issues, PR reviews/comment remediations, and multi-operator checkout calibration. Currently:
1. `skills/2-daily/daily-planner/SKILL.md` and `skills/3-weekly/weekly-planner/scripts/planner_core.py` require an existing weekly plan baseline (`pivot_daily` at `:734`, defaulting to `temp/planner/` unless `--plan-file` is passed) and an explicit `--team-issue <n>` integer (`:1842`) to publish a device comment.
2. There is no `--mode ledger` (or daily ledger issue resolver) in `planner_core.py` to search for today's `"Daily Work Ledger — YYYY-MM-DD"` GitHub issue, file it if absent (when authorized via `--publish-ledger`), locate the most recent previous workday's `"Daily Work Ledger — *"` issue and its comments to carry forward unfinished operator items, or aggregate what work is already checked out by whichever operator started earliest today.
3. `daily-planner/SKILL.md` does not chain `/recon` (to trace active seams and N+1 downstream state for assigned issues/PRs) and `/debug-mantra` (to verify live ground truth of PR review comments, failing CI checks, and claimed checkouts before recommending action), nor does it document auto-detection across Native Forge mode (`releases.db` + `utils/hq/`), Vendored `.xyz/` mode, and zero-dependency GitHub fallback mode.

Root cause: `planner_core.py` was built around a local file baseline (`weekly-plan-*.json`) plus an optional manual `--team-issue` comment sink (`GH-1184`), leaving daily GitHub-native continuity and multi-operator checkout visibility unimplemented. Fixing this in `planner_core.py` and `skills/2-daily/daily-planner/SKILL.md` (with `skills/3-weekly/weekly-planner/SKILL.md` architecture notes) extends the single shared planner engine without creating a new skill or script.

## Plan

1. **Extend `skills/3-weekly/weekly-planner/scripts/planner_core.py` with Daily Work Ledger mode (`--mode ledger`) and repo-mode auto-detection (`--repo-mode {auto,forge,vendored,gh-only}`):**
   - Update `main()`'s pre-dispatch `get_open_prs` guard (`planner_core.py:1871`) from `if args.mode not in {"stalled", "daily"}:` to `if args.mode not in {"stalled", "daily", "ledger"}:` so a missing/broken repo slug or offline `gh` records a `failed` coverage gap (and exits 3 when `--publish-ledger` is set) instead of raising an uncaught `RuntimeError`.
   - Add `resolve_repo_mode(repo_root, explicit_mode)` with precedence `--repo-mode` CLI > `XYZ_DAILY_LEDGER_MODE` env > `device_config.json` `daily_ledger_mode` > `auto` detection (`forge` when `releases.db` and `utils/hq/hq.sh` exist at `repo_root`, `vendored` when `.xyz/` exists at `repo_root`, and `gh-only` otherwise). Preserve installed-engine vs target-repo separation (`--repo-root` points to the target checkout). In `forge` mode, reuse `get_release_milestones` / `ingest_weekly_intake` (zero new `sqlite3.connect` calls, honoring `GH-777`) to enrich tasks with release milestone burndown, PRS scores, and active marathon/jog queues; in `vendored` mode, resolve `.xyz/` device identity and scan `.tick/` active claims (`<repo_root>/bin/tick` or `.xyz/bin/tick`) plus local worktrees without requiring `releases.db` or a weekly baseline; in `gh-only` mode, operate purely from GitHub issues/PRs and local git refs without requiring `.xyz/` or `releases.db`.
   - Add `find_or_create_daily_ledger_issue(repo_root, slug, date_local, ledger_issue_arg, create_if_missing, coverage)`:
     - Use a shared day timezone (defaulting to `America/Los_Angeles` or `XYZ_LEDGER_TZ`, overridable via `--ledger-tz`) so all operators share one calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`.
     - If `--ledger-issue <n>` is passed, resolve issue `#<n>` directly via `gh issue view`. Otherwise query `gh issue list -R <slug> --search '"Daily Work Ledger — " in:title sort:created-asc' --state all --limit 100 --json number,title,state,url,body,createdAt,author` and filter by exact regex `^Daily Work Ledger — (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})$`.
     - If discovery fails or hits the 100-item cap (`status != "ok"` in `coverage`), refuse to create a new issue (exit 3 on `--publish-ledger`) so a failed/truncated lookup never files a blind duplicate.
     - **Canonical tie-break & concurrent-create reconciliation:** If multiple issues exist for `date_local` (e.g. two operators raced on creation), the **lowest issue number (`min(number)`)** is canonical; the engine still reads comments across all duplicate same-day issues so no operator comment is lost, and surfaces a warning pointing duplicates to the canonical issue. When today's issue is absent and `--publish-ledger` is set, create `"Daily Work Ledger — <date_local>"` and immediately re-run the discovery query to reconcile against any concurrent creation (selecting `min(number)`). Without `--publish-ledger`, run strictly read-only on GitHub and write `temp/planner/daily-ledger-<date>.{json,md}`.
     - Resolve `previous_ledger` as the most recent ledger issue whose parsed title date `< date_local` (ordered by parsed title date descending, tie-broken by `min(number)`), and fetch both `today_ledger_comments` and `previous_ledger_comments` via paginated `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{slug}/issues/{num}/comments?per_page=100` (`read_stalled_comments` pattern at `:1635-1652`).

Cross-verify every cited `#N` / `GH-N` against live `open_issues` and `prs`: only confirm an item closed/merged when `open_issues` and `prs` coverage are `ok` (if either lookup failed or truncated, mark unverified rather than silently dropping carryovers).
     - **Newly assigned issues, PR reviews & comment remediations:**
       - Assigned issues: open issues where `operator` is in `assignees` not already in prior-day continuation.
       - PRs awaiting review: open non-draft PRs where `operator` is in `reviewRequests` (adding `reviewRequests` to `get_open_prs` at `:334`; requested team slugs are surfaced with a `team:<slug>` note since team membership is not expanded offline).
       - PR comment & CI remediations: for open PRs authored by `operator`, flag `reviewDecision == "CHANGES_REQUESTED"`, `ci_status == "FAILURE"`, and unresolved inline review threads fetched via a bounded GraphQL query (`gh api graphql` querying `repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads(first:100){pageInfo{hasNextPage} nodes{isResolved isOutdated}}` for the operator's open PRs; if `hasNextPage` is true or the query fails, record a `truncated`/`failed` coverage entry).

Combine with live GitHub signals (`in progress`/`🚧` labels, issue assignees, open PR `headRefName` + authors) and this device's local git/worktree/`.tick` scan (`scan_local_checkout`), explicitly labeling provenance (`verified-ledger-claim`, `github-label-or-pr`, `local-device-only`) and flagging collisions with `operator`'s candidate queue.
   - **Authenticated ownership check on comment `PATCH` (`sync_daily_ledger_comment`):** Query authenticated GitHub user (`auth_login` via `gh api user -q .login`). Before `PATCH`ing an existing comment matching `<!-- daily-ledger:<operator>:<device>:<date_local> ... -->`, verify that `comment["user"]["login"].lower() == auth_login.lower()` AND `operator.lower() == auth_login.lower()` (unless `--allow-delegate-comment` is explicitly set for a bot/service account that authored that comment); if another GitHub user authored the comment or `--operator` does not match `auth_login`, refuse to `PATCH` (exit 3) so a forged marker or mismatched `--operator` can never overwrite another teammate's comment.
2. **Update `skills/2-daily/daily-planner/SKILL.md` (and `skills/3-weekly/weekly-planner/SKILL.md` linkage notes) to chain `/recon` and `/debug-mantra` into the Daily Work Ledger workflow:**

3. **Verify in a disposable full clone and record receipts under `TESTS-RESULTS/`:**

body:
## Executive summary

PR branches write the RELEASES ledger (`releases.db`, `releases.sql`), so any two open PRs that touch it conflict as soon as one lands. This issue proposes a default for the harness, and for XYZ-forge itself as a dogfood project: PR branches do not write the ledger, and the post-landing reconcile on the integration branch is its only writer. Each vendored repository can change that default in its own configuration.

- High: in LTVera-Pandas on Nov 13th, 5 of 22 open PRs change the ledger, and 43 of 88 commits on `development` since Nov 1st touch it.
- High: the same ledger-only conflict on LTVera PR BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas#992 was re-created seven times on Nov 12th and 13th, once by each landing.
- Medium: the vendored `.gitattributes` marks `releases.sql merge=binary`, so two PRs that add different rows still conflict.
- Medium: in XYZ-forge, 318 of about 1,400 commits from Sep 25th to Oct 25th touch the ledger, and 66 of them are code or docs changes carrying a ledger edit (#1224).

Filed as an idea to revisit. It does not authorize implementation.

## Proposal

- [ ] **Default: a PR branch does not change `releases.db` or `releases.sql`.** Whatever the PR would have written (rating, lifecycle move, row for a new capture doc) is written by the landing reconcile (`wave_reconcile.py`, merge-cleanup Phase 5) on the integration branch, through `releases_app.py`. This extends #1131 decision 1 (the landing session writes the ledger, one writer at a time) and #1340 rule C3 (rows checkpointed on the primary before dispatch) to every ledger write.
- [ ] **Per-repository setting.** A key in the repository's existing `.pdda-mode` file, for example `LEDGER_WRITES=landing` (default) or `LEDGER_WRITES=branch` (current behaviour). The skills that write the ledger today (start-task, express, merge-cleanup, prs-backfill, weekly-planner) and the PDDA coverage checks read it.
- [ ] **Coverage checks follow the setting.** Today `pdda.sh roadmap-coverage` makes a missing row for a new `1-INBOX` or `2-WORKING` doc an error in the pre-push gate (#1340 D-a), so a PR that adds a capture doc must also add a row. Under `landing`, a missing row in a PR branch is expected; the check runs after the landing reconcile instead.
- [ ] **Dogfood first in XYZ-forge**, then vendored repositories opt in. LTVera-Pandas is the first candidate (BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas#737 proposes the same thing on the LTVera side, from Oct 9th).

## Not proposed

- Moving the ledger out of git, or making GitHub issues the source of truth. The committed `releases.sql` is the offline backup; #1224 explores the larger move separately.
- Changing what the ledger records, or the rating schema.

## Open questions

- Which writes, if any, must stay on the branch? One candidate is a rating needed before admission, which #1340 already moves to pickup on the primary.
- Under `landing`, what happens if a reconcile fails after a merge? Today `express-reconcile-failed` plus `resume` covers express; merge-cleanup needs the same.

Related: #1131, #1224, #1340, #1345, BinoidCBD/LTVera-Pandas#737.

body:
Results of a `/10days` sweep run on 2026-11-11 against `origin/development @ 966290ddd`, covering **Steps 0–6.5 only**. The run stopped before Step 7: no branch, commit, push or lane execution, and no capture docs, roadmap rows or plan files were written. Planner and preflight both ran with `--dry-run`.

**Result: nothing could fire.** 10 of 58 issues are still valid work. 8 of those have no capture doc in `PROJECT/2-WORKING`, and the other 2 have outdated contracts. The planner's own single wave held 4 lanes (#1171, #670, #1296, and one it didn't name). None of them could fire for this sweep: #670 and #1296 are excluded below, and #1171 is outside the window.

## Window and intake

- **Window:** last 10 days (`scan-issues.sh 10 0`), 58 open issues.
- **Step 2:** no issue had a `3-COMPLETED` doc, so all 58 went to evaluation.
- **Step 3:** 12 record issues (10 `merge-batch`, 2 `radar`) were excluded as not work items. 6 read-only subagents evaluated the other 46.
- **Clone:** disposable full clone at `~/marathon-clones/10days-2026-11-11-HiQS-Labs-XYZ-forge-20261111-141211`.

## INCLUDE, ranked by effective PRS score

No issue has a manual `ovr` override, so every effective score equals `calc`. "Provisional" means the issue had no stored rating and was scored with the skill's rubric.

| Rank | # | Summary | pri/sev/appeal/effort | calc | Provisional | Preflight (dry-run) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #1243 | consult: a negated claim word still sets off the false "no citation" flag | 65/60/70/75 | 270 | no | **exit 4 STALE**: the doc's probes only catch the part PR #1406 already fixed |
| 2 | #1423 | relay-drive: exit 4 when the relay file is under a gitignored path | 60/60/60/90 | 270 | yes | exit 6, no doc |
| 3 | #1421 | board_sync: opt-in read of `agent_session_activity` | 60/60/90/60 | 270 | yes | exit 6, no doc |
| 4 | #1422 | Trim AGENTS.md below 32 KiB (it is 42,768 bytes now) | 60/60/90/60 | 270 | yes | exit 6, no doc |
| 5 | #1188 | Jog lease check reads the driver heartbeat (L2 only) | 60/60/60/60 | 240 | yes | exit 6, no doc |
| 6 | #1315 | skills-army-hq: `--migrate-legacy` preview and apply disagree | 60/45/50/85 | 240 | no | exit 6: the doc is in `1-INBOX` |
| 7 | #1344 | Leftover work from #1340 item 1 (doc reader, 5 small review fixes) | 80/60/50/35 | 225 | no | **exit 4 STALE**: probes only catch what PR #1350 delivered |
| 8 | #1322 | AGENTS.md: auto-fix ladder | 60/30/60/60 | 210 | yes | exit 6, no doc |
| 9 | #959 | skills-army-hq: label drifted links as DRIFT, list unmanaged dirs | 40/40/50/55 | 185 | no | exit 6: the doc is in `1-INBOX` |
| 10 | #961 | skills-army-hq: any device may publish | 20/15/50/85 | 170 | no | exit 6: the doc is in `1-INBOX` |

Evaluators confirmed in the code that each bug is still present:
- `utils/py/relay_drive.py:682-686`
- `utils/py/releases_app.py:5138` (process-liveness check only, no heartbeat)
- `utils/py/board_sync.py:133-163`
- skills-army-hq `scripts/sync.py:289/296` and `SKILL.md:121/145`
- `utils/py/consult.py:71-77`
- `utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:1242`
- `wc -c AGENTS.md` returns 42768

The two STALE results are **not** "already landed". In both cases the old contract's probes only check the part that already merged. The evaluators found the leftover defects and proposed new probes, so the fix is to rewrite those contracts, not to close the issues.

## Step 6.5 overlap check and wave order

If all 10 had valid contracts, these pairs would have to run in different waves:
- **#1322 and #1422** both edit `AGENTS.md`.
- **#1243 and #1188** both edit `relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh`.
- **#959 and #1315** both edit skills-army-hq `scripts/sync.py`.
- **#959 and #961** both edit skills-army-hq `SKILL.md`, `README.md` and `references/recovery.md`.
- **#961 and #1315** share no listed file, but #1315's evidence points at `intake.py:571`, which is in #961's list, so they are kept apart too.

That gives:
- **Wave 1:** #1243, #1423, #1421, #1422, #1315, #1344
- **Wave 2:** #1188, #1322, #959

Four Wave 1 lanes touch `utils/py/`. The planner flags lanes that share that folder as coupled lanes, so treat Wave 1's concurrency as advisory.

- [ ] Rerun preflight once per issue, then run the overlap check again.

Contracts that would be auto-drafted and need operator review: #1423, #1421, #1422, #1188, #1322, #959, #961, #1243, #1344.

#1315 and #959 have no `## Acceptance` section in the issue, so preflight's acceptance check (GH-400) will report `unknown` for them.

  - #1254: PRs #1369 and #1379 merged; what remains needs live runs.
  - #1383: PR #1385 merged; what remains is a push-coalescing rework plus live measurement under #1386.
- **Already being worked on (open PR or draft):**

  - #1409 (PR #1413)

  - #670: an operator deferred it, and #1419's PR #1420 covers the same reviewer restriction.
- **Not a lane-sized build** (umbrella, tracking, arc, spike, audit, idea list or live proving run): #237, #522, #1175, #1298, #1310, #1325, #1328, #1329, #1333, #1340, #1353, #1356, #1358, #1359, #1360, #1366, #1386, #1400, #1418.
- **Records, not work items:**
  - Merge-batch logs: #957, #1313, #1323, #1374, #1375, #1380, #1394, #1398, #1408, #1412
  - Radar reports: #293, #1352

## Problems with the skill and tooling found during the run

1. `skills/3-weekly/10days/SKILL.md` Steps 2 and 3 call `releases_app.py roadmap show <N>`, but that subcommand doesn't exist (valid choices: sections, sync, reconcile-state, list, render, add, rate, pickup, repoint, update, move). The run used `roadmap list --json` instead. The skill should be updated.
2. The ledger entries for #1295 and #1344 point to `1-INBOX` docs, but both docs are actually in `2-WORKING`. The planner also flags the GH-1344 doc as missing its ledger pointer.
3. `scan-issues.sh` exits 2 when `gh` is not on PATH (it lives at `/usr/local/bin` on this host). Preflight also reports `codex=missing agy=missing` as an advisory.
4. `marathon-plan.sh --dry-run --deep` took more than 10 minutes because it dry-runs preflight for every ready row in the ledger (623 items), not just this sweep. It returned exit 4 (drift present, 220 items held). The skill's Step 5 note covers filtering the output afterwards, but not the runtime cost.
