body:
## Current execution scope — 2026-11-07

PR #1367 is merged into development (`8e52a06051f35007334285a589b024f0aa22dbe6`), including Jog completion and the North Star proportionality principle. The operator now authorizes start-task for one bounded remediation. First task: align the witnessed-red paragraph with the existing new/materially changed decision-gate scope, and clarify that the appendix priority ordering does not exempt controls from proportionality review. Preserve containment and the GH-831 test policy. This PR addresses part of checklist items 1/2 only; the umbrella remains open. Broader recommendations below are not blanket implementation approval.

## Original audit scope (completed)

Audit restrictions whose operational burden may exceed the concrete harm they prevent. Research, review, and remediation planning only, in this issue. That original research request did not authorize implementation. The new start-task authorization above permits ordinary intake, an isolated task clone, verification, independent QA and a PR for the selected slice.

Triggered by Jog closeout friction in #1365: landed work remained parked because approval ancestry did not cover finishing changes. That issue owns the Jog implementation and the general proportionality wording. This audit examines other surfaces and must not duplicate it.

## Initial assessment preserved from the discussion

Rules introduced after real incidents have sometimes expanded into permanent requirements for unrelated, low-risk work. Initial candidates (hypotheses pending deeper recon):

- **No new tests:** preventing suite/gate proliferation may also prevent lasting regression coverage for new capabilities. Prefer controlling runtime and redundant coverage while allowing justified cases in existing suites.
- **Mandatory plan plus final review:** appropriate for consequential designs, potentially excessive for straightforward local fixes. Scale separate plan review to design uncertainty and risk.
- **Two-to-three-line intake threshold:** line count is a poor risk proxy; a four-line doc correction may require an issue/capture while a dangerous one-line change looks trivial. Consider PR-only records for bounded reversible changes.
- **Universal witnessed-red rule:** deliberate negative controls are valuable for new/materially changed decision gates; requiring them for every existing assertion is disproportionate. Align AGENTS with the narrower GUIDING-PRINCIPLES wording.
- **Two-attempt parking:** preserve bounded execution but distinguish identical failures from verified repairs and temporary provider outages; examine existing recovery paths before proposing another.
- **Promotion quiet window:** potentially blocks throughput as tests and parallel work grow. Consider immutable release-candidate qualification only if actual freeze cost warrants the larger change.
- **Friction-last ordering:** GUIDING-PRINCIPLES explicitly ranks implementation speed/operator friction last; it may undermine the proportionality principle being implemented in #1365.

Retain destructive-command restrictions, concurrent-work protection, and disposable full clones for mutation-heavy tests: these address documented data loss.

Proposed calibration: a blocking rule should identify the harm prevented, why existing controls are insufficient, and a practical recovery path. Administrative discrepancies should normally remain visible without blocking reversible work.

## Recon Map — workflow restriction proportionality

**Revision:** `cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430`. **Mode:** grep/read-only source inspection; no codebase-memory tool available. **Lanes:** A/C policy, entry paths and boundaries; B/D retry state and recovery; D/C gates and promotion, plus parent reconciliation of contradictions and reviewer prompts. Three parallel read-only agents supplied source-cited findings; the parent reviewed and reconciled them. This is an analytical review, not a relay approval or runtime qualification.

The user explicitly requested **one GitHub issue only**. This issue therefore contains the Recon Map and separate remediation plan instead of local map/plan/capture files. No repository writes, tests, workflow dispatches, queue mutations, PRs, or implementation were performed. Existing untracked GH-1365 capture was left untouched.

### Subject and change class

Subject: policy and enforcement that can block intake, independent review, retries, push, and promotion despite bounded/reversible work.

Change class: proposed policy/contract calibration, with separately gated runtime refinements. No new authority store or persisted schema is proposed. Any later move to issue-less execution, new retry state, or release-candidate authority requires its own authority/consumer assessment before implementation.

### Corrections to the initial assessment

- **Plan QA already has a simple-change exception.** Start-task explicitly permits skipping it with a brief reason; final QA still applies. The universal double-review recital obscures this. First fix discoverability, not invent another exemption. [skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:50](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md#L50); [skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:194](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md#L194).
- **Retry recovery exists.** Both Python drivers expose configurable caps and force; Jog offers retry, retry-build, and retry-gate. The actual weakness is coarse fire accounting and confusing interaction between queue retry and the lane budget—not absence of recovery.
- **Every push does not rerun the full gate.** Docs/tiered selection and exact-SHA full-gate receipt reuse already exist. Do not add another cache or blanket bypass. [githooks/pre-push:257](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/githooks/pre-push#L257); [githooks/pre-push:286](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/githooks/pre-push#L286).
- **“No new tests” is broader in prose than the observed mechanisms.** Express requires an existing registered suite; registry consistency is not itself a prohibition on new assertions. No generic enforcement of the entire policy was established.
- **One marathon and one driver lock are different.** The former is portfolio/WIP policy; the verified lock protects a Git clone family. Changing work selection must not weaken the lock.
- **Express is not a way around fresh clones.** It also requires a fresh task clone. [utils/py/express.py:662](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L662).
- **Generic reviewer prompt restrictions are confirmed; the particular incident's exact effective prompt was not reconstructed here.** The thread reported difficulty reading historical revisions; source supplies a plausible mechanism, not a replay of that session.

### Seams and entry paths

| Seam | Entry / owner and next consumer | What breaks or becomes costly |
|---|---|---|
| Proportionality | [GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md:153](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md#L153) → reviewer heuristics; [skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:202](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md#L202) → reviewer dispositions | Friction-last language conflicts with commensurate-complexity guidance and can make advisory concerns into mandatory scope. #1365 owns the general correction. |
| Intake | [PROJECT/PDDA.md:253](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/PROJECT/PDDA.md#L253) → [ROUTER.md:49](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/ROUTER.md#L49) → start-task capture/rating/admission at [skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:97](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md#L97) and [skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:219](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md#L219) | A line-count proxy triggers records and downstream identifiers; removing issue IDs without adapting consumers is not a prose-only change. |
| Distribution | [utils/pdda/pdda-sync-manifest.conf:16](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/pdda/pdda-sync-manifest.conf#L16) includes PROJECT/PDDA.md → [utils/pdda/pdda-sync.sh:300](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/pdda/pdda-sync.sh#L300) | A global intake edit propagates beyond Forge. Prefer an explicitly scoped Forge adoption exception unless shared policy is intentionally changed. |
| Review access | [relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:1067](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh#L1067) allows narrow non-mutating probes, but [relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh:1172](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh#L1172) says NEVER run Git; [utils/py/marathon_drive.py:3104](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/marathon_drive.py#L3104) also bans it | Historical content verification requires extra hand-packaging; blanket Git prohibition conflates reads and writes. Preserve harness commit ownership and worktree safety. Related #1092. |
| Express admission | `cmd_run → cmd_check → cmd_docs → cmd_ledger → cmd_land`, [utils/py/express.py:1502](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L1502), [utils/py/express.py:1057](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L1057) | Fixed authority-skill names refuse even editorial changes; admitted skill edits require local approval attestation and candidate ancestry. [utils/py/express.py:100](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L100), [utils/py/express.py:224](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L224), [utils/py/express.py:717](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L717). |
| Review-to-publication | Express calls [utils/py/express.py:139](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L139) → [utils/py/relay_attest.py:395](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/relay_attest.py#L395) | Approval must cover candidate tree except named transcript paths; seeded-artifact review cannot qualify. Unlike Jog bookkeeping, this guards direct integration-branch publication. Do not copy Jog's relaxation here. |
| Attempt budget | [utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1229](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/marathon_drive.py#L1229) / [utils/py/relay_drive.py:247](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/relay_drive.py#L247) → fire file → result outcome → Jog queue | Timestamp/fire count ignores failure cause and whether a correction was made. Cap defaults to 2 but is configurable; force exists. |
| Queue recovery | [utils/py/releases_app.py:4922](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/releases_app.py#L4922) retry writer → [utils/py/jog_run.py:2178](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/jog_run.py#L2178) pending selector → driver cap | Requeue clears queue failure/lease and moves to tail, but does not reset the clone's fire budget; the next dispatch can repark. |
| Gate routing | [utils/ci-route.sh:23](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/ci-route.sh#L23) mapping → [utils/ci-route.sh:358](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/ci-route.sh#L358) test escalation → [utils/ci-route.sh:468](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/ci-route.sh#L468) tier → pre-push | Unmapped code and unclaimed test paths use full gate; mapped test/code co-touch already has an exception. Full fallback is appropriate for genuinely unknown impact. |
| Receipt reuse | [validate.sh:1589](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/validate.sh#L1589) → [utils/py/gate_receipt.py:65](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/gate_receipt.py#L65) → [githooks/pre-push:286](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/githooks/pre-push#L286) | Exact valid full receipt skips repeat full gate; partial/marathon/legacy evidence does not qualify. Preserve this existing mechanism. |
| Promotion | [.github/workflows/wave-reconcile.yml:37](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/.github/workflows/wave-reconcile.yml#L37) → [utils/py/wave_reconcile.py:666](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/wave_reconcile.py#L666) → [utils/py/hosted_lane_publish.py:184](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/hosted_lane_publish.py#L184) → [utils/py/wave_reconcile.py:2496](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/wave_reconcile.py#L2496) | Development checkout, metadata, publishing and receipt consumers are coupled. Removing a quiet-window sentence alone cannot safely implement independent candidate qualification. |

### State, contracts, failure, and rollback today

- **Agent policy:** Markdown instructions influence agents; a recommendation in prose is not automatically an executable gate. Start-task has no generic executable driver identified in this bounded search. PDDA doc-ready LLM advice is opt-in/advisory ([utils/pdda/pdda-doc-ready.sh:11](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/pdda/pdda-doc-ready.sh#L11)), whereas selected marathon QA has actual strict checks ([utils/pdda/check_marathon_qa.py:240](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/pdda/check_marathon_qa.py#L240)).
- **Retry state:** `.tick/attempts/<lane>` records fires; Jog execution state/receipts record dispatch outcome; `jog_queue` holds pending/running/parked/failed/completed projection. There is not one unified retry counter. Execution state is saved before dispatch and projected afterward ([utils/py/jog_run.py:628](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/jog_run.py#L628), [utils/py/jog_run.py:670](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/jog_run.py#L670)). Rebuild preserves history with a fresh token while retaining the lane budget ([utils/py/jog_run.py:1003](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/jog_run.py#L1003)).
- **Lock state:** lock identity derives from Git common directory; live holders refuse concurrency, dead holders can be reclaimed ([utils/py/rtl.py:966](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/rtl.py#L966), [utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1385](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/marathon_drive.py#L1385)). This is a data-integrity protection, not administrative ceremony.
- **Express refusal:** diagnostic telemetry plus SystemExit ends the invocation; audit logs are not a retry queue ([utils/py/express.py:302](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L302)). Unchanged reruns fail again. Existing tunable size/multi-subsystem options must be considered before new bypasses; the two-local-commit limit remains a separate proxy ([utils/py/express.py:681](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L681), [utils/py/express.py:779](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L779), [utils/py/express.py:1531](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/express.py#L1531)).
- **Verification contracts:** AGENTS' universal assertion-red wording ([AGENTS.md:123](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/AGENTS.md#L123)) conflicts with the narrower new/materially changed decision-gate wording ([GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md:85](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md#L85)). No-new-suite/new-gate restrictions and narrow existing-suite edit allowance are at [AGENTS.md:161](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/AGENTS.md#L161).
- **Promotion receipts:** committed telemetry/provenance bind tested SHA, gate, mode and width. Reader checks landing ≤ tested ≤ current HEAD, with historical Small-suite membership interpreted at the tested commit ([utils/py/wave_reconcile.py:554](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/wave_reconcile.py#L554)). Main's sequential macOS check and pre-promotion parallel qualification are distinct stages, not proven redundant work.
- **Existing rollback:** policy/routing edits can be reverted without format migration; completed publications cannot be “unpublished” by reverting an admission rule. Retry histories and receipts must remain intact. Novel persisted retry fields or candidate-branch semantics would add compatibility obligations and are not approved by this plan.

### Step N+1 downstream checks

- **Consumer progress:** Jog selects pending only. Parked is an intentional stopped/actionable state, not an automatically retried transient state. `jog retry` restores selection, but the lower-level cap may refuse again. Recovery owner is an explicit retry/force/budget decision; no infinite automatic retry was found on this path.
- **Retry after approval:** marathon resets attempts on attested approval before post-approve execution ([utils/py/marathon_drive.py:2834](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/cff1d0a16c2c9a6eb073b99ef259d3658aea1430/utils/py/marathon_drive.py#L2834)). A closeout failure must not be treated as another failed build.
- **Promotion race:** publisher preserves receipts through bounded push retries and one recomputation; `--only-receipted` defers newcomers rather than qualifying them from old evidence. Further races fail actionably; no unbounded loop found in this path.
- **Parameter role:** suite lists and queue status predicates select work; they do not generate new work candidates. No solver parameter change proposed.
- **Coexistence:** near-term recommendations retain receipt/queue formats and existing writer ownership. Any richer retry or candidate-release design must inventory old/new readers before writes; that compatibility is not established here.

### Unknowns and bounded cutoffs

| Unknown | Why it changes the decision | How to settle before implementing dependent work |
|---|---|---|
| Present gate duration, freeze delays, cap-related parks, Express refusal frequency | Source proves possible burden, not its frequency or cost | Sample existing run logs/Actions timing, merge timestamps and refusal records; record denominator and actual operator delay. No new telemetry service. |
| All issue-less execution consumers | A “PR-only” exception could break pickup, rating, reconciliation or closeout | Trace those writers/readers with one representative small task; retain existing IDs until this is complete. |
| Safe revision-reading commands in each reviewer runtime | Git has configurable helpers and more than purely read-only subcommands | Inspect harness/provider permissions and demonstrate narrowly scoped historical reads without commit/index/worktree/config mutation. |
| Invocation environment overrides | A packet may override caller LANE_MAX_ATTEMPTS | Trace preflight packet generation before promising universal cap propagation. |
| Full promotion merge consumer | Candidate qualification may conflict with actual merge admission | Read promotion/merge-cleanup callers before any candidate branch design. |
| Distributed policy/skill revisions | A local correction may be overwritten or unintentionally spread | Inspect source manifests and deployed revisions; use canonical publication flow, no hand-copy. |
| Existing suite sensitivity for proposed changes | Located coverage is not executed proof | Run appropriate existing suites/manual controls in a disposable full clone during later implementation. |
| Ongoing #1365 changes | Concurrent work may resolve wording or alter line locations | Rebase audit decisions on its final merged diff before pickup. |

Cut off at live cost-history collection, full outer-loop retry consumers, exhaustive external installations, and promotion merge implementation. No claim that a bounded search proves absence of every hook. These unknowns deliberately limit the scope of the plan below.

**Current-state radius:** Forge agents and reviewers, PDDA intake/distribution, Express direct publication, Jog/Marathon retry and clone locks, local gate routing/receipts, and hosted development-to-main qualification.

---

## Sharpened remediation plan

### Decision and blast radius

**First use existing escape paths and reconcile contradictory instructions; then change only the controls shown to impose avoidable cost.** Avoid another generic approval framework, retry engine, policy registry, or monitoring service.

Beyond the current-state radius, this plan introduces more explicit agent discretion for low-risk work and potentially broader reviewer observation capability. Those are meaningful behavior changes even when implemented as prose. Near-term wording is **Easy** to reverse; review-access and direct-publication eligibility are **Costly until their containment boundaries are proven**. Promotion redesign remains deferred.

### Ordered, prioritized checklist

1. [ ] **P0 — Reconcile with merged #1367 and correct overstatements.** The North Star proportionality change is present. Preserve the appendix's containment-first tie-breaker and add a scope clarification: it does not exempt controls from the North Star cost/benefit assessment. Make start-task's opening recital show its existing simple-plan exception and preserve final QA. Distinguish advisory findings from blocking failures; each blocker should name concrete consequence and supported recovery. **Acceptance:** a simple reversible change can skip plan QA with a reason, while a containment/schema change retains design review; no duplicate policy owner or new gate. **Rollback:** revert wording. **Dependency:** satisfied by merged #1367; inspect current source before pickup.

2. [ ] **P1 — Separate red-control clarification from the test-policy decision.** Align the witnessed-red scope now. Any permission for previously unpinned regression cases amends GH-831's dated operator decision and requires an explicit decision before implementation. Compare committed manual checks (durable, but not automatically rerun) against existing-suite regression cases using recurrence and maintenance cost; do not assume automated cases win. Keep current no-new-suite/no-new-runner and existing-suite restrictions until that decision. Use new/materially changed decision gates as the mandatory red-control scope; unchanged coverage reruns do not require fresh mutations. **Acceptance:** worked examples admit a useful regression case, reject redundant suite proliferation, and retain negative evidence for a changed gate. No test added merely to enforce policy. **Verification:** manual policy/reference review; later behavior edits use relevant existing suite. **Rollback:** revert policy; no schema changes.

3. [ ] **P1 — Make independent review capable of observing its evidence.** Coordinate with #1092; trace and reconcile the generic no-Git prompt and marathon reviewer scope. First use existing safe read facilities or supply pinned historical content automatically. If needed, permit only proven non-mutating revision inspection, preserving prohibition on commits, index/config/ref writes and mutation-heavy tests in worktrees. Do not grant unrestricted Git or weaken containment to avoid packet preparation. **Acceptance:** reviewer can independently inspect a specified historical file/diff without a separate operator packaging turn; mutation attempts still fail; unverified claims remain explicitly labeled. **Verification:** existing gh397/gh505/gh681 coverage where applicable plus a focused manual historical-read/mutation-refusal check in isolation. **Rollback/stop:** restore prompt/access if writes escape or claimed evidence cannot be reproduced; retain review records. No provider-permission bypass.

4. [ ] **P1 — Replace the intake line-count proxy with a bounded Forge exception.** Define low-risk by behavior, scope, reversibility and coordination needs rather than line count. Preserve full intake for features, experiments, multi-step work and consequential one-line changes. Start with a Forge-local adoption exception; do not silently export it via shared PDDA. **Before enabling PR-only execution:** finish pickup/rating/reconciliation/closeout consumer inventory; otherwise retain identifiers and simplify only duplicate prose. **Acceptance:** a multi-line editorial correction avoids disproportionate planning, a dangerous one-line change does not; normal consumers can complete the chosen lightweight path. **Verification:** representative manual intake-to-closeout trace and applicable existing PDDA checks. **Rollback:** restore prior policy; retain already-created issue/PR history.

5. [ ] **P1 — Connect existing retry recovery to the actual stopping layer.** Make diagnostics distinguish queue requeue, builder retry, gate-only retry, exhausted lane fires and closeout failure; point to supported bounded recovery appropriate to that caller. Document existing configurable cap/force rather than building a new retry service. Preserve pre-token cap refusal and clone locks. **Acceptance:** pending → cap-parked → explicit authorized recovery advances or gives a precise remaining blocker; a plain requeue is never described as resetting lane fires. **Verification:** existing Jog adapter cases and a manual Python-path cap/force check if needed; legacy Bash lane-cap suite alone is insufficient. **Rollback:** diagnostics/docs revert without deleting attempt history. Defer failure-class accounting until frequency data justifies it.

6. [ ] **P2 — Audit Express's risk proxies before broadening direct publication.** Replay an identical bounded editorial diff across an authority skill and an ordinary skill, and across two versus three local commits, to establish which refusals are intentional versus incidental. Reconcile effect-based skill guidance with filename-list implementation. Prefer the normal PR path if cases are rare. If change is justified, retain explicit operator authorization, final-head evidence, canonical writers, repository identity and fast-forward publication checks. **Acceptance:** equivalent approved risk gets consistent treatment; behavioral authority changes remain on the reviewed path. **Verification:** existing gh267 Express coverage and focused negative controls in a disposable clone. **Rollback:** restore admission before publication; already-landed changes require ordinary revert/fix. **Do not transplant Jog completion relaxation to pre-merge publication.**

7. [ ] **P2 — Measure and repair only demonstrated gate-routing gaps.** Use existing history to identify frequently changed unmapped paths/test-only escalations and actual full-gate time. Extend the existing subsystem map only where callers/coverage establish isolation. Keep kernel/containment/gate/mixed or unknown impact on full selection; retain exact-SHA receipt reuse. **Acceptance:** named safe examples select intended suites, unsafe/mixed paths still escalate, receipt mismatch still refuses reuse, no new runner/cache. **Verification:** existing ci-route/gh35 tier suites with changed-behavior assertions and negative controls. **Rollback:** restore mappings. Do not equate Markdown or TESTS-RESULTS paths with harmlessness: this repo contains executable evidence artifacts.

8. [ ] **P3 — Leave promotion freeze, fresh full-clone isolation and one-marathon policy unchanged unless measured costs warrant separate decisions.** Clarify work-selection policy versus the per-clone lock. Measure actual freeze time/blocked merges before tracing immutable-candidate design through workflow, publisher, receipt and merge consumers. Measure clone overhead before simplifying naming/lifecycle; never solve it by running destructive suites in shared worktrees. **Acceptance for further work:** a demonstrated cost and complete consumer/rollback map, not a speculative throughput benefit. **Rollback boundary:** no novel candidate semantics published/promoted until compatibility is established.

### Review disposition and completion criteria

- Initial blanket “mandatory plan QA” claim: **corrected**; exception already exists.
- Initial “retry cap blocks recovery” framing: **narrowed** to queue/budget mismatch and raw-fire accounting.
- New receipt cache / universal gate bypass: **rejected as redundant or overbroad**.
- Global no-new-tests repeal: **rejected** in favor of justified regression cases without suite proliferation.
- Promotion architecture and automatic reset-on-code-change: **deferred**; the latter could turn unrelated edits into unlimited retries.
- Blanket Markdown exemption and unrestricted reviewer Git: **rejected**.
- Independent analytical review: three read-only recon lanes plus parent source reconciliation; **not a formal implementation approval**.
- Only the selected wording slice is in execution. The test-policy amendment awaits an explicit operator decision; remaining items retain their discovery/authorization conditions. Unknown-dependent items are discovery-gated, not implementation-ready promises.
- Completion of this audit means this issue contains the initial assessment, corrected source-grounded map, prioritized checklist, bounded unknowns, and acceptance/rollback criteria. It does **not** mean any restriction has been removed or any suite has passed.

Related: #1365 (Jog and general proportionality), #1092 (review evidence access), #453 (governance ownership).

## Astra adjudication of K3 review — 2026-11-07

Read [K3's complete review](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1366#issuecomment-6717286760) and current source after #1367. Decisions below qualify the checklist above.

- **Accept: witnessed-red alignment.** Import the existing “new or materially changed decision gate” scope into AGENTS; unchanged-suite reruns do not need fresh mutation. Preserve falsifiable checks, manual evidence and no-new-suite policy. Selected for this task.
- **Accept with scope: appendix priority.** K3 is right that the hierarchy is inside doc-review heuristics and the containment-vs-speed tie-breaker. Add a pointer to the North Star proportionality assessment rather than reorder protections. Selected for this task. The original assessment overstated the ranking as global.
- **Accept: test-policy authority and manual evidence.** Committed manual evidence is durable; the distinction is automatic recurrence detection. Amending the dated GH-831 restriction is a separate operator decision, not implied by this first task. No new tests/guards proposed here.
- **Accept diagnosis, reject prescribed wrapper as established protection.** The reviewer prompt conflicts with itself. However, `utils/git-sandbox-guard.sh` probes config/config.lock writability and then runs the supplied command; it intentionally enables mutation and does not filter Git commands. A voluntary wrapper also cannot prevent direct Git access. A command-name allowlist alone does not settle option/config/helper side effects. Reuse existing safe reads/pinned artifacts first; a new guard must independently earn its cost and comply with the no-new-gate rail. “Costly until proven otherwise” remains the repo default for relay containment changes, not a claim that a prose clarification itself is expensive. This task does not broaden reviewer capabilities.
- **Accept narrower retry seam, qualify the one-file-read fix.** Queue retry leaves the build budget untouched; retry-build accumulates it; retry-gate does not redispatch a build. But queue and execution roots can differ, and the effective cap can be overridden in invocation environment. Do not read a guessed primary-clone attempt path or claim every requeue must repark. First resolve execution identity/lane/cap through existing records; if unavailable, report the uncertainty. Prefer an advisory warning over adding another refusal. `retry-build` alone does not clear an exhausted cap.
- **Accept reduced intake cost, reject skipping pre-execution consumers.** Decision 6 moves ledger creation to pickup; measure today's residual issue/capture cost. PARKED is observation intake, not proof of issue-less execution. A PR appears after implementation, so claiming pickup/rating “would never see it” assumes away the requirements being changed. Retain the bounded start/pickup/admission and closeout inventory before implementing PR-only work.
- **Accept minor confirmations:** authority-skill list, raw fire counter and existing receipt reuse. Keep Express's direct-publication boundary distinct from Jog's delivered-work bookkeeping.

Source anchors at merged revision: [Git guard](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/8e52a06051f35007334285a589b024f0aa22dbe6/utils/git-sandbox-guard.sh), [North Star and appendix](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/8e52a06051f35007334285a589b024f0aa22dbe6/GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md), [queue retry](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/8e52a06051f35007334285a589b024f0aa22dbe6/utils/py/releases_app.py#L4922), [execution/retry ownership](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/8e52a06051f35007334285a589b024f0aa22dbe6/utils/py/jog_run.py#L514).
title: Audit: calibrate workflow restrictions to risk and reduce disproportionate delivery burden

body:
## Sharpening from #1358 reviews — before pilot activation
Native timing, existing bounded subprocess execution and prototype intent/receipt semantics are reuse, not new capability. The gain is equivalent LTVera monitoring/alerts with less paid model usage and no reliability regression. #1168 implementation readiness and the deployed health contract remain unverified.

Before a timed pilot, map schedule → bounded HTTP observation → healthy/degraded/unknown classification → alert/no-alert transition → receipt → next wake. Each row names a real command/API, state/effect owner, positive witness, failure control and bounded failure decision. Record single-cycle evidence before starting a longer run; no fictional generic runner or notification API.

Replay actual current-monitor failures first if records exist; otherwise label timeout/malformed-response/duplicate-wake controls as injected. Never describe an injected failure as a production incident. Distinguish a legitimate in-flight probe/notification from a missed poll using pinned timeouts and overlap policy; a fresh timestamp alone does not prove progress.

Route schedule/overlap issues to #1168, endpoint/schema mismatch to LTVera's owning issue, and alert delivery/dedup to the selected notifier owner before activation. Missing credentials, unidentified old task or unknown external effect blocks cutover; maximum three preparation repair rounds per blocker, no blind resend after an uncertain alert.

Choose pilot duration from response-state/alert/restart coverage and required host availability, not a borrowed factory soak. Count changed health/alert transitions versus unchanged healthy polls. Accept existing Grok job if migration fails output/availability parity or maintenance offsets savings. Shadow produces no external alerts; enable replacement only after verified old-owner disable. No claim of host-loss detection from a same-host process.

## Objective
Plan a small task-agnostic supervisor script that can replace selected paid Grok Bot scheduled jobs. **Operator-selected first pilot: LTVera app Health Check API endpoint monitor.** Research and plan only; no schedule activated, monitor invoked, notification sent, credential accessed, or Grok task disabled.

## Medium-depth recon (2026-11-07)
Forge source inspected at `3bf02f73ce0cb11a82f970357209980f808ccb3c`, using rg/direct reads. No new source-of-truth decision is made here.

| Confirmed seam | Source | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ONE shared local scheduler already has an owner | #1168, live OPEN | Coordinate with that contract, not another scheduler. Per-job opt-in, lock, receipt, missed-run policy; current scope excludes existing-job migration |
| Primitive tool list hard-coded | utils/py/harness.py:29,317-360 | note/summarize/probe/idle/plan-draft are not arbitrary jobs; probe is local-no-network |
| Rules adapter separates judgment from scheduling | harness.py:186-221 | Deterministic jobs need no LLM every wake |
| Intent, receipt, consumption and quarantine | harness.py:41-78,131-149,1263-1288,1420-1458,1511-1525 | Missing receipt does not justify replay of external effects |
| Prototype sandbox permits output/temp writes only | harness.py:1384-1402 | Do not loosen it to make generic maintenance work |
| Bounded process-group runner exists | utils/py/proc_group.py:3-18,108 onward | Reuse for subprocess jobs if needed |
| Deterministic hourly scan already exists | utils/hq/hourly-global-scan.sh:21-41; install-hourly-scan.sh:21-59 | Timing/reporting alone is not new capability |
| Some tasks require native app tools and one writer | skills/3-weekly/task-sync/SKILL.md:298-325 | Not every Grok/native task can migrate to a local script |

#1248 remains a prototype whose timed soak driver explicitly is not a scheduler install (TESTS-RESULTS/2026-10-29+GH-1248/driver.py:1-5). #1200/#1175 own factory decisions; this issue owns generic-job requirements and selective migration, not another factory queue.

Read-only filtered LaunchAgents metadata showed existing Git Pulse/RebalanceOS schedules, no matching XYZ/HQ/Grok/supervisor job. Current-project T3 scheduled-task list returned empty. Neither proves external Grok tasks absent. No arguments, secrets or payloads published.

## LTVera pilot grounding
Read a local LTVera-Pandas clone at `dd76b53d9de611bc067280ff4357a87ac02f5668`, not a deployed version claim:
- app/api/routes/health.py:159-179 defines /health (module describes /api/health), reports status/app/environment/checks; returns 503 if required checks fail.
- :132-155 can POST a RAG query as part of health evaluation; a poll can have downstream work/cost. Some unconfigured probes return true rather than proving those services healthy.
- scripts/check_buffer_server_health.py is a broader existing CLI covering buffer/BQ/GCP/WP; it is not automatically equivalent to the requested app endpoint monitor.

**Unresolved before pilot:** exact existing Grok task and URL, route mount/deployed version, cadence/timezone, authentication reference, body/field expectations, allowed downstream probe cost, timeout, failure/recovery thresholds, alert channel and current notification policy. No secret should be copied into issue/config. Actual Grok usage and bills unknown; zero savings claimed.

## Triangulate research card
CELL: irreversible × crossing when schedule/effect ownership moves; full lenses, bounded medium recon.
GROUND: #1168 scheduler → named job → bounded execution → observation/intent → receipt → next wake/alert.
FALSIFY: greenfield scheduler premise disproved by #1168; arbitrary executor premise disproved by primitive tool/sandbox limits; safe blind retry disproved by quarantine semantics; every-wake LLM requirement disproved for deterministic checks.
SMALLEST: HTTP monitor under existing scheduling ownership, optional model only for separately justified diagnosis.
UNKNOWN: live #1168 implementation readiness and deployed LTVera/Grok contract.

## Alternatives and decision
1. Existing scheduler plus an existing equivalent HTTP monitor command, if verified: smallest.
2. Minimal Python task runner under #1168 exposing named job, timeout, lock and receipt: only shared behavior actually needed by pilot.
3. Bounded optional model diagnosis on a confirmed incident: defer until deterministic alerting demonstrably insufficient.
4. Keep Grok job if connector/availability or maintenance costs outweigh savings.
5. Generalize whole factory primitive into arbitrary plugins: reject for pilot.

An always-on existing host may suit monitoring better than a sleeping Mac. Select host from required coverage and available infrastructure; do not create remote hosting/network exposure by implication.

## Ordered plan — apply ground → falsify → shrink in every phase
1. **Inventory and contract.** Capture current Grok job configuration safely, exact endpoint/body schema/cadence, notification effects, authentication references and actual cost baseline. Falsify HTTP-200-only success with malformed/degraded responses and optional checks. Select one real monitor, not all scheduled tasks.
2. **Ownership and mechanism.** Confirm #1168 implementation and explicit ownership for schedule, observations and notifications. Falsify scheduler-alone sufficiency against overlap, sleep/missed ticks and alert-after-effect crash. Use native timing and smallest named HTTP handler; no arbitrary model-generated shell, new backlog, ledger or plugin framework. Agree host/interval based on required coverage.
3. **Report-only shadow.** Compare equivalent observations with current monitor; suppress all replacement external alerts. Ground expected health/degraded/unknown states. Falsify with timeout/DNS/TLS failure, 503, malformed/empty body, wrong app/environment, missing checks, duplicate/overlap, stale output and restart. HTTP read retry may be bounded; notification retry requires dedup/reconciliation, never blindly duplicate. Choose enough opportunities plus restart/control coverage, not an arbitrary multi-day soak.
4. **Single-owner cutover.** Read back that exact old notification-producing task is disabled before enabling new alerts. Falsify dual-writer risk across a scheduled boundary. Explicit activation approval per job; no inherited broad send authority. Rollback disables new owner, reconciles uncertain sends, then re-enables old owner. Keep original job configuration recoverable.
5. **Evaluate and extend only on evidence.** Compare detection/recovery latency, missed checks, false positives, duplicate alerts, operator minutes and actual usage including downstream endpoint work. Falsify claimed savings with maintenance burden. Only generalize shared execution contracts after a second real job needs them. Clone cleanup #1359 remains separate authority; report-only clone census could later be another handler, never automatic deletion by this pilot.

## Plan triangulate card
GROUND: scheduler and runner responsibilities separated; existing ownership respected.
FALSIFY: generic script does not imply connector parity or uptime while host asleep; endpoint polling is not proven free/read-only in downstream behavior.
SMALLEST: one deterministic LTVera monitor with typed observation and durable alert transition state.
SKIPPED WITH TRIGGER: semantic diagnosis when rules demonstrably insufficient; generic job adapters when a second inventoried task needs them; cleanup effects only after #1359 safety/ownership plan.

## Acceptance and planned red controls
- [ ] Nonempty pilot contract matches actual Grok job and deployed endpoint; no guessed cadence/URL/auth/cost.
- [ ] Valid healthy/degraded/unknown observations distinguished; 200 HTML, empty body, missing expected checks or stale response cannot pass.
- [ ] Declared timing coverage met and missed checks reported; sleeping-host limitation explicit.
- [ ] Duplicate wake/overlap yields at most one intended observation/alert effect; no claim of exactly-once external delivery without destination support.
- [ ] Timeout bounded; subprocess cancellation affects owned group only if subprocess used.
- [ ] Consecutive-failure/recovery thresholds and alert dedup match approved policy; missing send receipt becomes uncertain rather than blindly retried.
- [ ] Shadow emits no external notifications; cutover proves one effect owner; rollback rehearsed without duplicates.
- [ ] Deterministic routine checks make zero model calls; cost comparison includes actual old usage and new host/endpoint/intervention costs or explicitly UNKNOWN.
- [ ] Existing checks or manual red controls plus provenance under TESTS-RESULTS/<date>+GH-1360/; no new suite/gate. This plan specifies controls; none claimed executed.
- [ ] Independent review verifies contract, ownership and results before broader migration.

## Investment rubric (#1358)
Gain: replace paid model-driven polling with equivalent bounded deterministic monitoring. Discriminating test: actual LTVera semantics plus interruption/alert controls. Value: measured savings and operator effort, not genericity; no runtime build commitment until task inventory and #1168 readiness justify it.

## Bounds and rollback
Planning reversible; scheduling/effect ownership migration is Costly and crossing. No changes to existing scheduler, sandbox, secrets, messages or application during recon. #1328 repair ceiling applies to implementation; predeclare numeric time/usage budgets and escalation before activation. Do not silently change #1168's no-auto-retry/missed-run contract.

## PRS proposal
- pri 65: concrete recurring paid monitor selected by operator.
- sev 30: efficiency/reliability opportunity; no current incident established.
- appeal 50: neutral.
- effort 45: single pilot plus safe cutover; actual inventory may reduce scope.
Unstarted implementation intake; no ledger row. Related #1168, #1248, #1200, #1175, #1188, #1358, #1359.
title: Task-agnostic supervisor: scope a deterministic scheduled-task replacement for paid Grok Bot jobs

body:
## Sharpening from #1358 reviews — before implementation
Existing discovery, provenance classification, fresh teardown and targeted retirement are baseline capabilities, not new deliverables. The gain must be a demonstrated missing completion-to-retirement connection or a corrected false preservation—not a higher deletion count.

Before an hourly pilot, freeze a per-producer transition map: completion/publication → retirement invocation → fresh classification → retire/preserve → next reconciliation. Each row needs its actual supported command/API, owner, positive witness, relevant refusal control, and failure disposition. Begin with naturally observed dirty/active retention, missing reminders/invocations, installed drift and T3 omissions; do not fabricate disposable workload.

Route tag equivalence to #1247, retained landing clones to #748, deployed drift through Skills Army HQ, and unknown T3 ownership to preserve pending its API contract. Three repair rounds maximum per unresolved blocker under #1328; no safety override to obtain a green census. An active long job is a reason to preserve, not stale merely because an hourly scan elapsed.

Time the pilot by actual completion/retirement and state-change coverage, not 24/48 hours by default. Record scans with changed dispositions separately from unchanged scans. Proceed to periodic reconciliation only if event-driven repairs leave measured residual misses; otherwise omit it. Unknown eligibility is not a cleanup failure and cannot become an automatic delete decision.

## Objective and scope
Determine why completed jobs leave clones, then repair demonstrated lifecycle gaps without weakening preservation. Research/plan only; no deletion or schedule activation. This issue coordinates existing defects #1247 (remote-identical tags) and #748 (retained landing clones); their fixes remain with those owners.

## Medium-depth recon — 2026-11-07
Read-only source/device pass at `3bf02f73ce0cb11a82f970357209980f808ccb3c`. No teardown, gate, fetch, or safe-delete verdict performed. Paths below are relative to this revision.

| Confirmed seam | Source | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Published retirement is an agent closeout instruction | skills/1-hourly/start-task/SKILL.md:320-359 | No universal completion callback |
| Marathon prints retirement guidance inside cost-summary output with early-return paths | utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1812-1841 | Reminder may disappear; reminder is not retirement |
| Express prints guidance | utils/py/express.py:1208 | Another handoff rather than automatic disposal |
| Jog exit cleanup releases supervisor lock | utils/py/jog_run.py:2147-2155 | Does not dispose of clones |
| Exact-path published retirement already validates provenance and fresh state | skills/2-daily/merge-cleanup/scripts/merge_cleanup.py:1712-1752 | Reuse this implementation |
| Default roots plus same-origin primary siblings; immediate-child scan | skills/2-daily/merge-cleanup/scripts/scan_clones.py:26-83,1169-1194 | Primary siblings covered; nested T3 roots not covered by default |
| Preserve dirty/ignored/stashed/unpublished/active/dependent/unknown state | scan_clones.py:1085-1155 (same directory) | Retention may be correct |
| Trash full clones; Git-remove worktrees | merge_cleanup.py:1069-1114 (same directory) | Tidiness does not immediately reclaim disk |

Bounded Path.iterdir inventory: 26 immediate Forge Git checkouts in the primary's Documents/GitHub parent (including primary/current runner), two T3 worktrees under ~/.t3/worktrees/XYZ-forge. Zero matching immediate checkouts under Documents/GH Repos or marathon-clones; Documents/GitHub Repos absent. These are NOT device-wide or eligible-for-deletion counts.

Five samples inspected with `git --no-optional-locks`: gh805-test-value has one dirty entry; gh1317 pilot, gh1325 gate and gh1160 sample clean/no stash but remote recovery and live ownership unverified; current gh1356 runner clean but active. Clean does not establish disposable.

Installed script byte comparisons differ despite identical SKILL.md: deployed scanner/teardown lack repository GH-1308 containment/origin rechecks. This is deployment drift, NOT proven cause of accumulation. Deploy through Skills Army HQ only. Bounded LaunchAgents literal search found no merge-cleanup/retire-published references; wrappers/other schedulers remain unknown.

## Triangulate — research
- CELL: irreversible × crossing for eventual retirement; full lenses, medium-depth bounded trace.
- GROUND: creation/completion callers → handoff → discovery → provenance/session checks → fresh teardown.
- FALSIFY: “all leftovers are missed cleanup” disproved by dirty and active examples; “primary sibling root omitted” disproved by default_scan_roots.
- SMALLEST: ownership/disposition census before another cleaner.
- UNKNOWNS: per-folder completed-job attribution, remote recovery, handles, T3 lifecycle API, scheduler wrappers.

## Ranked explanations, not one universal root cause
1. Missing lifecycle invocation: strongest source evidence; correlate actual terminal jobs before attribution.
2. Correct safety preservation: observed dirty/active samples; never weaken checks to improve deletion counts.
3. Producer/discovery mismatch: nested T3 paths outside default discovery and safe roots; ownership contract required before any change.
4. Ref provenance false positive: existing #1247; inspect current classifier at scan_clones.py:549-642 and its fetch at :570.
5. Installed code drift: confirmed, accumulation impact unknown.
Temporary landing leaks remain #748.

## Triangulate — plan
- GROUND: exact-path retire_published_checkouts plus refresh_for_teardown already exist.
- FALSIFY: “hourly deletion fixes the class” fails against correctly preserved and externally owned checkouts.
- SMALLEST: fix demonstrated closeout omissions, then periodic reconciliation for missed eligible cases.
- SKIPPED: T3 removal until ownership/session contract verified; permanent trash purge and automatic disposal of ambiguous state.

## Ordered plan (each phase repeats ground → falsify → shrink)
1. Census roots, registered worktrees and completed jobs by producer; record owner and exact disposition or UNKNOWN. Falsify completeness against git worktree registry and known T3 paths. Produce nonempty sourced inventory, not an age-based deletion list.
2. Trace real completion records to attempted retirement for start-task, Express, Jog/Marathon, gate helpers and T3. Challenge “missing invocation” against actual preservation receipts. Link #1247/#748; select only evidenced repair sites. Root-cause statement must name origin, fix site and why upstream/downstream is inappropriate.
3. Implement minimal verified integration and deploy matching cleanup code through Skills Army HQ. Prefer existing per-job exact-path retirement over new remover. Decide shared completion hook only if traced producers have a common truthful terminal event.
4. Evaluate hourly reconciliation after event-driven fixes. Start report-only; deduplicate unchanged exceptions. Any later action requires explicit owned roots, fresh inspection and established authorization. Do not expand deletion authority through discovery alone.
5. Verify through existing suites in disposable full clone or recorded manual checks; publish findings and retention outcomes. Prove that changing state between scan and teardown is rechecked.

## Acceptance and falsification
- [ ] Every observed checkout gets sourced ownership/disposition or explicit UNKNOWN; empty/failed scan cannot pass.
- [ ] At least one real completed-job chain explains an omission or a correct preservation; folder age is not root-cause evidence.
- [ ] Eligible completed task retires through existing mechanism or produces an actionable preservation reason.
- [ ] Dirty, ignored evidence, stash, unpublished refs, active session, dependent worktree, unknown query and out-of-root controls all preserve.
- [ ] State changed after scan refuses teardown; remote-equivalent/local-only/differing-tag cases handled under #1247.
- [ ] Repeated reconciliation causes no duplicate effects or repeated unchanged alerts.
- [ ] Existing checks/manual red controls and provenance committed under TESTS-RESULTS/<date>+GH-1359/ during implementation. No new suites/gates.
- [ ] Retired/preserved counts and space-in-workspace vs space-in-Trash reported separately.

## Investment rubric (#1358)
Capability: reduce missed cleanup without losing protected state. Test: real completion-to-disposition evidence plus safety controls. Decision value: first determine whether caller repair suffices; only add periodic execution if residual missed cleanup warrants it. No hourly remover approved by this research.

## Unknowns and cutoff
No full safety scan, lsof, remote PR/ancestry attribution, T3 internals or wrapper scheduler trace. These are next targeted lookups, not assumed absent. Main review question: per-producer closeout vs shared hook, resolved by terminal-event ownership.

## PRS proposal
- pri 70: recurring operator effort and workspace accumulation.
- sev 45: cleanup errors can affect unique work; no loss observed in this pass.
- appeal 50: neutral.
- effort 45: bounded lifecycle audit and targeted repairs; T3 integration separately sized.
Unstarted implementation intake; no ledger row. Planning is reversible; actual disposal crosses data-loss boundaries and requires current safety proof.
title: Housekeeping: trace and close task-clone retirement gaps without weakening preservation checks

body:
## Three must-meet rubrics — select the work mode first

**Rubric 1 — Meaningful capability gain:** name the observed baseline, the new capability and why it removes a real bottleneck. Repeated component checks, more PRs or longer runtime are not gains. Choose exactly one mode:

### Rubric 1A: Formal Unattended Work

Use this mode for formal unattended execution of real work. The deployed system, real workload, observation, approval arrangement and stop/recovery controls must be established before the window starts. **Autonomous bounded repairs allowed and recorded; human assistance disclosed; no silent cap, permission, safety, or gate changes.** Adapt and continue rather than stopping for routine issues.

**Standing authorization ladder for Rubrics 1A and 1B — apply in order without reopening the authorization question each session:**

1. **Recover and continue.** Use an existing supported retry, recovery or alternative path within the recorded time, spending and attempt limits. No additional approval is needed.
2. **Make the smallest routine repair.** If recovery is insufficient, repair the task, code, configuration or environment within the issue's scope and standing operator/repository authorization. Use required isolation, record the reason and change, run the existing relevant checks and continue. Supervisor/configuration repairs are not a special stopping class. If they change the running version, record the new version and its verification, then continue.
3. **Keep independent work moving.** If the affected item remains blocked within its budget, preserve its state and advance eligible independent work. Never bypass dependencies or locks.
4. **Escalate only the actual boundary.** Ask the operator when the action needs per-PR merge approval, increases caps or spending, requires new credentials/accounts/destinations or network exposure, is destructive or irreversible, or disables/bypasses a gate or safety control. Otherwise a needed routine repair within these limits is already authorized; do not manufacture a per-session permission decision.

title: Post-Batch-2 qualification: prove between-wake orchestration before a bounded unattended run

body:
## Objective

Execute the first full-scale, end-to-end "real" run of the software factory flywheel under an autonomous supervisor outer-loop. This campaign targets XYZ Forge's most critical severe issues, exercising all newly landed factory primitives:
1. **Decoupled Backlog Pickup (GH-1345 / PR #1351)**: Intake rows stay as pure Markdown until active execution begins.
2. **Cap-Stall Resilience (GH-1332 / PR #1354)**: Relay-receipt-only tails accepted by `jog retry-gate` when lanes stall at turn caps.
3. **Preflight Admission Contracts (GH-1298 / PR #1355)**: Verified contracts required before token spend.
4. **Autonomous Supervisor Outer-Loop (#1328)**: Continuous multi-hour monitoring, autonomous stall intervention, and 3-gate bounded repairs.

---

## Target Issues

| Issue | Title | Severity & Impact | Primary Artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#1296** | launch packets fail preflight on stale artifact path or missing contract | **High** — Blocks automated planning loops from emitting launchable lanes. Integrates candidate work from PR #1324. | `utils/py/harness.py` |
| **#1288** | `factory-primitive tick` fails (rc 1) under macOS sandbox profile | **Critical** — Blocks all stateful fuzzing campaigns from running sandboxed. | `contracts/profile-long.sb`, `utils/py/harness.py` |
| **#1287** | fuzz supervisor no-new-signal stop never fires due to echoed tokens | **High** — Wastes 10,000 mutation steps on trivial argparse syntax errors instead of true novelty. | `tools/supervisor.py` |
| **#1254** | outer loop declared supervision (`FACTORY_SUPERVISED=1`) & cache warmth dispatch | **High** — Borrows Clodex supervision contract and prompt-cache token efficiency. | `utils/py/harness.py` |
| **#1344** | governance finishing work (Tasks 10, 9, 8, 7) | **High** — Solves chronic Radar doc-reader resolution and close-at-merge authority gaps. | `utils/pdda/pdda.sh`, `utils/py/wave_reconcile.py` |

---

## Supervisor Outerloop: "Prompt" Plan for Sub-Session Execution

The following plan is copy-pasteable for any autonomous agent (Antigravity, Claude Code, or Codex) acting as the **Supervisor Outer-Loop**.

```markdown
### AGENT INSTRUCTION: Supervisor Outerloop Orchestration

You are the **Supervisor Outerloop** for XYZ Forge Software Factory Flywheel Batch 2.
Your goal is to initialize the run environment, dispatch worker sub-sessions across the target issues, monitor progress autonomously over several hours, intervene safely when lanes stall, and qualify landed PRs.

#### Phase 1: Environment & Disposable Runner Setup
1. Export supervision:
   ```bash
   export FACTORY_SUPERVISED=1
   ```
2. Create a clean disposable task clone for runner execution:
   ```bash
   RUNNER_ROOT="/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GitHub Repos/XYZ-forge-runner-batch2-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
   git clone /Users/noelsaw/Documents/GitHub Repos/XYZ-forge "$RUNNER_ROOT"
   cd "$RUNNER_ROOT"
   git checkout development
   bash githooks/install.sh
   ```

#### Phase 2: Decoupled Intake Pickup & Preflight Verification
For each candidate issue (#1296, #1288, #1287, #1254, #1344):
1. Pick up from `PROJECT/1-INBOX/` into the roadmap ledger (exercising GH-1345 cutover):
   ```bash
   python3 utils/py/releases_app.py roadmap pickup --issue-num <NUM>
   ```
2. Verify preflight dry-run passes:
   ```bash
   python3 utils/py/swarm_preflight.py --dry-run PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-<NUM>-*.md
   # Expect: exit 0, stale=0, blocked=0, ambig=0
   ```
3. Enqueue into Jog serial queue:
   ```bash
   python3 utils/py/releases_app.py jog add GH-<NUM>
   ```

#### Phase 3: Launch Worker Sub-Session
Dispatch the Jog runner in the disposable clone in the background:
```bash
nohup python3 utils/py/releases_app.py jog run \
  --target-root "$RUNNER_ROOT" \
  --reviewer codex \
  --builder agy \
  > temp/jog-batch2-runner.log 2>&1 &
RUNNER_PID=$!
echo "Jog runner launched with PID: $RUNNER_PID"
```

#### Phase 4: Autonomous Monitoring & Push-Along Protocol (Handsfree Watchdog)
Arm a 10-minute recurring wake loop for up to 3 hours (using `/schedule` or native background tasks):
1. **Liveness Check**:
   - Check if `RUNNER_PID` is alive: `kill -0 $RUNNER_PID`.
   - Inspect queue status: `python3 utils/py/releases_app.py jog list`.
   - Inspect tail of `temp/jog-batch2-runner.log` and active execution receipts.
2. **Cap-Stall Intervention (PR #1354 Resilience)**:
   - If an item transitions to `cap-stalled` or stops advancing:
     a. Inspect the worktree branch head (`git -C <wt> log -1`).
     b. Trigger an independent cross-model review turn (e.g. Codex) over the uncommitted/committed changes.
     c. If approved, commit an approval receipt (`relay-system/<lane>/RELAY.md`).
     d. Execute `python3 utils/py/releases_app.py jog retry-gate GH-<NUM>`.
     e. Observe that `_is_relay_receipt_tail` accepts the tail and cleanly advances to gate execution!
3. **Three-Round Repair Bounding (#1328 Rule R2)**:
   - If an environmental or code blocker emerges, diagnose and attempt at most 3 repair rounds.
   - If unresolved after 3 rounds, run `python3 utils/py/releases_app.py jog skip GH-<NUM> --reason "<blocker>"` and file/update the tracking issue.
4. **Heartbeat Logging**:
   - Log progress note to `temp/handsfree-batch2-status.md`.

#### Phase 5: Landing, Hosted Qualification & Receipt Capture
1. When a lane completes with an approved PR:
   - Verify hosted CI runs: `gh pr checks <PR_NUM>`.
   - Reconcile via merge-cleanup: `python3 utils/py/wave_reconcile.py --pr <PR_NUM>`.
2. Commit results receipts and telemetry under `TESTS-RESULTS/$(date +%Y-%m-%d)+GH-BATCH2/`:
   - `SUMMARY.md`
   - `provenance.jsonl`
   - Telemetry cycle time and cost receipts.
3. Post closeout comments on each completed issue.
```

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Disposable runner clone initialized with `FACTORY_SUPERVISED=1` and pre-push hooks active.
- [ ] At least 3 critical issues picked up from `PROJECT/1-INBOX/` via `releases roadmap pickup` with ledger rows created at pickup time (GH-1345 cutover verified).
- [ ] Preflight dry-run verifies `stale=0, blocked=0, ambig=0` on all picked up candidates.
- [ ] Jog runner executes serial lanes in isolated worktrees.
- [ ] At least one cap-stall or review handoff exercised using `jog retry-gate` accepting a relay-receipt tail (PR #1354 verified live).
- [ ] Outer loop adheres strictly to #1328 (3-gate rubric, max 3 repair rounds per blocker).
- [ ] PRs created with green hosted CI checks and verified landing evidence.
- [ ] Results summary and provenance committed under `TESTS-RESULTS/`.
title: Flywheel Batch 2: autonomous supervisor outerloop run across critical targets (#1296, #1288, #1287, #1254, #1344)

## Observed

| Claim | Command | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| The flywheel's bottleneck is shifting from build capacity to verification capacity, but the loop is not instrumented, so gate value and cycle time are anecdotal | Review of PR #1351 (GH-1345 cutover) + this repo's gate stack (pdda, gh308 frozen-twin guard, hosted CI, claim-validated QA receipts) | The #1298 arc records strong per-run evidence (Phase 0 spike, planning soak, ATE campaign) but no longitudinal metrics: no cycle-time series, no gate-escape rate, no receipt-freshness signal |
| Machinery exists that no ordinary consumer can reach | Claim-validated review of PR #1351, finding 1 (P1) | No-row issue discovery was added only inside `init_from_prs`; `Engine.compute()` and the admission census still enumerate ledger rows only, so after decision 6 a fully specified unstarted issue is invisible to normal planning |
| The meta-machinery verifying the code is itself rotting | PR #1351 committed receipt `relay-system/2026-11-07/gh1345-cutover-qa.md` vs the GitHub review at head `bfebc42` | Receipt says Approved/PASS over "+560/-164 across 20 files", which matches no commit in the PR (commit 1 alone is +689/-164 across 23 files), and it sits next to a Changes-requested review with a P1 blocker |
| Start paths apply two different rating contracts | Same review, finding 2 | `express.py` `cmd_ledger` writes via `roadmap add` (placeholder-tolerant) while `roadmap pickup` refuses placeholders; a `2/2/2/2` probe persisted through express |
| Idempotent pickup leaves a stale rendered link | Same review, finding 3 | Row reuse updates only `doc_path`; `raw_text` keeps the old inbox link that `roadmap_render()` replays |
| Rating policy is inconsistent between proposal acceptance and pickup validation | Same review, finding 4 + independent check | `parse_prs_proposal` accepts `50/50/50/50` with four distinct substantive rationales; pickup rejects it unconditionally. Also: the `hq park`-injected default proposal passes the proposal heuristic whenever the title is long enough to push all four rationales past 25 chars |

## Acceptance

- [ ] A recommendations report (capture doc + summary in this issue) proposing the next-gen flywheel changes, sized small/medium/large, each with blast radius and a falsifiable success measure
- [ ] A decision on the P1 discovery seam from PR #1351: either share the no-row discovery path with `Engine.compute()` / admission census, or document why factory planning stays on `init_from_prs` only
- [ ] A minimal metrics proposal for the loop: cycle time (issue filed → PR merged), gate escape rate (defects found after the gate that claimed to prevent them), and receipt-freshness (receipt diff-stat must match the reviewed range)
- [ ] A named answer to the coordination-cost question: the measured fixed cost per PR versus marathon throughput, and the minimum viable task size under the current gate stack

## Preflight Contract

```json
{
  "target": "XYZ-forge harness (docs + optional small instrumentation in utils/py/)",
  "gate": "pdda.sh run + covering suites for any touched code; no new suites (GH-831); frozen-twin guard green",
  "fix_probes": [
    "metrics ledger doc renders current cycle-time/escape-rate placeholders",
    "receipt-freshness check diffs receipt diff-stat against the reviewed range on demand"
  ],
  "artifacts": [
    "PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-<n>-NEXTGEN-FLYWHEEL.md (capture doc)",
    "recommendations report section in this issue"
  ]
}
```

## PRS proposal

- pri 65: Measurement converts flywheel anecdotes into tuning signal, unlocking every later optimization
- sev 30: Nothing is broken today; this is posture work that prevents wrong future bets
- appeal 70: Operator asked for these recommendations to survive the session that produced them
- effort 40: Mostly design and doc work plus one small deterministic receipt-freshness check

## Context

Filed from a PR review + design discussion with the operator on 2026-11-07. The current-cutover review verdict and findings live on the flywheel arc issue #1298; the immediate code findings (P1 + three should-fix) belong to PR #1351 / issue #1345 first — this issue is for what comes after. Related: #1340 (cutover umbrella), #1333 (decision evidence), #1200 (48-hour unattended experiment), #1224 (ledger outside the repo).

Live GitHub reads: **2026-11-07 19:54–20:03 UTC** (bounded acquisition interval; current observations, not reconstructed cutoff state). Coverage: 831 issues, 161 merged PRs since September 26, all 7 open PRs with paginated file lists, 1 radar board, 30 umbrella-title hits, 1,000 development runs reaching September 11, last 20 non-cancelled/non-skipped qualifying runs and their jobs.
