**Status: partially verified.** Code findings use the pinned tree and cited live reports. Umbrella scores and all-repository reopen counts remain unavailable where membership/history is incomplete; this is not an all-clear. Graph generation was September 1 and stale against this tree; exact source fallback was used. No runtime harness, full suite, server test, deployment, or remediation was run.

SOP: [docs/CI-CHURN-RECOVERY-SOP.md](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/5f6ef0dbc47bbf7c38bd88775d1074541975c904/docs/CI-CHURN-RECOVERY-SOP.md) (landed through [PR #880](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/880), merge `95e2cc66`). Current cadence is superseded by operator decision [#1131](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1131) and [PR #1142](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1142): local reconciliation; full hosted qualification at promotion.

Sink A: **not committed (local only)**. The complete text is also published in this run's GitHub issue so it survives other clones. Radar does not push. Full published run: https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1352. Existing live board: [#293](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/293); this run issue is a historical report, not another canonical checklist.


Development gained useful capabilities during this window: a native Kimi worker ([PR #1217](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1217)), better issue intake ([PR #1331](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1331), [PR #1335](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1335), [PR #1338](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1338)), and a first automated planning loop ([PR #1249](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1249), [PR #1274](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1274)). The team also repaired concrete safety and reliability problems, including merging work outside the approved selection ([PR #1227](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1227)) and overlooking older completed work ([PR #1311](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1311)). These changes are landed on development; this report does not claim that every installation has received them.

The practical constraint is still getting work through the whole process without human rescue. Maintenance represents 80.3% of classified-plus-unclassified non-machinery commits; feature work rose to 6.8% from 4.3% in the preceding equal window. That is a modest recovery, not a measurement of staff hours. Planning records still disagree with GitHub, a new skill-migration preview promises an action that execution refuses, and some generated launch packets cannot actually start. The likely cost is repeated checking, interrupted unattended work, and delayed delivery—not an observed customer outage or measured financial loss.

## Recommended next steps, in order

1. **Decide on a short stabilization cycle using the existing SOP.** The shared-file conflict threshold and maintenance-share threshold fire; this does not establish a current CI outage. Keep the already-approved promotion cadence. Success means recording the decision, owner, end date, and measurable exit conditions rather than silently imposing a freeze.
2. **Finish the work already underway before opening substitutes.** Review [PR #1351](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1351) at its explicit operator hold, and inspect [PR #1324](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1324) for the two readiness failures it covers. Keep [#1344](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1344)'s remaining readers and [#1296](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1296)'s missing contracts visible. After that cutover, address [#1332](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1332) item 2 in its agreed order. Success: a selected real task starts, finishes, and is recorded correctly without a hand-edited ledger or unnecessary rebuild.
3. **Make previews tell the truth.** Assign [#1315](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1315) to the Skills Army maintainer: use the existing ownership validation during preview as well as apply, or explicitly choose another supported ownership rule. Success: the unadopted-skill case is refused before promising migration, with a clear adoption remedy; supported adopted cases still work. Reuse existing verification assets; add no new suite or gate.

## Lens 1 — where commits went

These are commit counts, not effort, value, cost or productivity. Mechanical prefixes are an imperfect proxy; features often contain many fix and review commits. Automation commits are excluded from the work-mix denominator.

| Bucket | Current count | Current work share | Prior count | Prior work share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Harness | 753 | excluded | 334 | excluded |

| Run | 462 | 80.35% | 348 | 83.25% |

| Grow | 39 | 6.78% | 18 | 4.31% |

| Transform | 0 | 0.00% | 0 | 0.00% |

| Unclassified | 74 | 12.87% | 52 | 12.44% |


Proof: **1328 subjects = 1328 bucketed = 1328 `git rev-list --no-merges --count`**. Prior: **752 = 752 = 752**. Files: `temp/radar/current-subjects.txt`, `prior-subjects.txt`, `analysis.json`. Both nonempty. `/usr/bin/git log` used explicit offset timestamps and pinned SHA; non-merge commits reachable on development, including commits authored on feature branches. Thus commit dates are not all merge dates. Scoped conventional prefixes are accepted, including `plan(scope):`; reconcile and version-record families are machinery.

Adjusted read (only obvious intake/status/Jog/receipt prose moved from Unclassified to Harness; other uncertain subjects stay uncertain): Harness 801, denominator 527, Run 87.67%, Grow 7.40%, Unclassified 4.93%. Prior adjusted: Run 87.66%, Grow 4.53%, Unclassified 7.81%. This sensitivity check supports modest feature recovery and broadly flat maintenance dominance, not a precise trend in human effort.

Explicit `rgt:` adoption: **0 declarations in 831 issue bodies/label sets and 161 merged-PR bodies/label sets checked**. Seven issue bodies mention the classifier or future adoption; none declares its own work Transform. Comments were not exhaustively searched for declarations; uncovered comment-only adoption is unknown. Transform 0 is a declared-basis figure, not proof that no transformative work occurred.

Measurement defect: component-as-type prefixes occur repeatedly (`adapt`, `jog`, `intake`, `test-results`). Missing-colon-after-scope had no matches in these two subject files. Normalize authoring conventions rather than treating machinery volume as product growth.

Historical arc: four committed reports dated August 28, September 1, September 2, September 21 (24 days apart) were found. Their reported Run shares include 76.7%, 76.9%, 82.4%; the later [#1138](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1138) records October 18 at 82.0% Run / 3.4% Grow. The October report file is absent from this fresh development clone, although its issue and board preserve the narrative. Historical classifiers and denominators changed; these are observations, not a normalized time series. This run's identical-method adjacent windows are the safer comparison.

## Lens 2 — ranked current targets and historical repairs

Ranking is qualitative: practical interruption and already-approved work order. Blast radius and median repair cost were not measured, so no invented numerical score is shown.

### 1. RADAR-class-roadmap-ledger-drift — chronic; existing ID

Live members [#1333](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1333), [#1340](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1340), [#1344](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1344), [#1345](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1345) are OPEN. These are the current governance repair program; they do not replace older target history. GitHub and the planning ledger are separate representations of completion. Four ledger rows still say Queue / parked intake for CLOSED issues: #216, #255, #1075, #1087. The latest issue comments explicitly retain part of #1344 despite [PR #1350](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1350) landing. Do not equate one merged PR with whole-issue completion.

**Real-world implication:** the next agent can prepare work already completed, miss work still owed, or ask the operator to reconcile contradictory status. [PR #1350](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1350) provides the completion sweep/readers, but its remaining readers are named in [the current #1344 comment](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1344#issuecomment-6686849318). [PR #1351](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1351) implements row creation at pickup and is OPEN with an explicit operator-review hold. Do not duplicate it or call it done.

**Action/acceptance:** owner of #1340 verifies remaining readers and uses the existing completion sweep after the approved cutover; the four closed-issue rows no longer masquerade as live work. Read-only `releases check` on a scratch copy is structurally clean; it cannot validate business status against GitHub. No DB changes made. Claimed by #1340/#1298 work program; no verified release-band membership.

### 2. RADAR-retire-legacy — new feature validation gap, not proven old-functionality regression

[#1309](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1309) CLOSED; feature [PR #1312](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/pull/1312) landed November 1. [#1315](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1315) OPEN, filed 46m27s after the close. Its preview reports success while apply refuses `Invalid retirement`; it is too soon to count as a >24-hour declared-fixed return. Live report says the old folder remained and only a backup ZIP was created; no data loss was reported.

Mechanism at the pinned tree: [skills/3-weekly/skills-army-hq/scripts/sync.py:245](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/5f6ef0dbc47bbf7c38bd88775d1074541975c904/skills/3-weekly/skills-army-hq/scripts/sync.py#L245) `retire_legacy()` constructs the retirement action only under `if apply:`. [skills/3-weekly/skills-army-hq/scripts/intake.py:571](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/5f6ef0dbc47bbf7c38bd88775d1074541975c904/skills/3-weekly/skills-army-hq/scripts/intake.py#L571) `validate_receipt()` requires `name == "skills-sync-trinity" or name in receipt["state"]["skills"]`. Preview does not encounter that receipt validation. Existing validation already exists: extend its use, not a second installer. No post-window fix exists in the pinned current tip. title: Radar 2026-11-07: work is landing, but unreliable handoffs still require human rescue

body:
Child of #1340 (item 1 of 2). Groups #1340 **Tasks 10, 9, 8 and 7**: everything about deciding when an issue is *done*. It does not change when ledger rows are created (that is item 2, the cutover). The task text, file:line citations and Codex QA live in #1340; this issue does not restate them.

## Scope

1. **Task 10:** readers find a doc by issue identity (`gh_issue` frontmatter, else the `GH-<n>-` prefix), across all four `PROJECT/` folders; stored `doc_path` values become caches (G2). Decide whether #1339's 1-INBOX fallback in `utils/pdda/pdda.sh` is kept or folded in.
2. **Task 9:** the completion sweep: route closed issues by GitHub `stateReason` (`COMPLETED` → `3-COMPLETED`, `NOT_PLANNED` → `4-MISC`, else report), repoint existing rows only, never create a row, never close an issue (G3). Extend `roadmap reconcile-state` / `issue-doc-sync` and the existing `wave_reconcile` mover; keep the `SHIPPED … (PR #N)` badge `jog land` needs.
3. **Task 8:** the sweep also prints delivered-but-open candidates and closes nothing. If that is just a report mode of Task 9, it is built as that, not as a new tool. The human review of the 55 #1333 candidates is not part of this PR.
4. **Task 7:** the landing step closes an issue only with a recorded whole-issue coverage assertion, or a non-empty, fully checked Acceptance checklist; otherwise it posts one "delivered, left open because …" comment (G4).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A doc moved between `PROJECT/` folders breaks no reader that #1340 Task 10 lists (red on the base, green on the PR), recorded under `TESTS-RESULTS/`.
- [ ] One sweep run on a disposable clone clears stranded docs and stale `doc_path` values (before/after recorded), and a closed, never-started capture moves without gaining a row.
- [ ] A local Jog landing still finds its `SHIPPED … (PR #N)` badge after the sweep.
- [ ] The sweep lists delivered-but-open candidates and closes nothing.
- [ ] A one-phase partial delivery with neither proof stays open with one reason comment; either proof closes it (red/green).
- [ ] Existing suites covering pdda, wave-reconcile and jog pass on the final commit. No new test (GH-831).

## Not in scope

The cutover (item 2), the 55-candidate human review, #1332 item 2, Task 13.

## PRS proposal

- pri 80: first in the #1340 order (P2); Task 9's sweep and Task 10's readers gate the cutover.
- sev 60: docs, rows and issue state drift today, so finished work looks open and stale paths break readers. Recoverable by hand.
- appeal 50: no operator preference.
- effort 35: four related changes across pdda.sh, wave_reconcile.py, jog_run.py and releases_app.py, all extensions of existing code.

Refs #1340, #1333.

🤖 Filed by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) for the operator, 2026-11-04.
